Compliance · EU

Medical Device Regulation

Regulation (EU) 2017/745 · applies since 2021-05-26 · mandatory-for-scope · official text (free)

Applies to: Manufacturers of medical devices, including software that is itself a device, placed on the EU market.

A point here means: Article, numbered paragraph and lettered or roman point at every depth; Annex, its Parts, Sections and Chapters, and its numbered points. Art. 1 Subject matter and scope
Art. 1(1) Sets the regulation's scope: placing, making available, and putting into service of human-use devices, plus clinical investigations. Coming soon
Art. 1(2) Extends the regulation to listed non-medical product groups once common specifications apply, including their clinical investigations. Coming soon
Art. 1(3) Devices with medical and non-medical purposes must meet both sets of requirements cumulatively. Coming soon
Art. 1(4) Defines 'devices' as a collective term for medical devices, accessories and Annex XVI products. Coming soon
Art. 1(5) Empowers the Commission to extend the Annex XVI product list through delegated acts. Coming soon
Art. 1(6) Introduces the list of products excluded from this regulation.
Art. 1(6)(a) Excludes in vitro diagnostic devices covered by their own regulation. Coming soon
Art. 1(6)(b) Excludes medicinal products, judged mainly by their principal mode of action. Coming soon
Art. 1(6)(c) Excludes advanced therapy medicinal products. Coming soon
Art. 1(6)(d) Excludes human blood products and devices incorporating them, apart from paragraph 8 devices. Coming soon
Art. 1(6)(e) Excludes cosmetic products. Coming soon
Art. 1(6)(f) Excludes animal-origin transplants, tissues and cells, but covers devices using non-viable ones. Coming soon
Art. 1(6)(g) Excludes human-origin transplants, tissues and cells, but covers devices using non-viable derivatives. Coming soon
Art. 1(6)(h) Excludes products containing viable biological material or organisms to achieve their purpose. Coming soon
Art. 1(6)(i) Excludes food covered by the general food law. Coming soon
Art. 1(7) Devices with an integral in vitro diagnostic part fall under this regulation, with IVD rules for that part. Coming soon
Art. 1(8) Devices with an ancillary integral medicinal substance are assessed here; if the substance is principal, medicines law governs. Coming soon
Art. 1(9) Devices administering medicines fall here, unless sold as a single non-reusable integral combination governed by medicines law. Coming soon
Art. 1(10) Devices with ancillary non-viable human tissue are assessed here; principal action shifts governance to tissue legislation. Coming soon
Art. 1(11) States this regulation is specific Union legislation for the purposes of the EMC directive. Coming soon
Art. 1(12) Devices that are also machinery must meet more specific machinery safety requirements where relevant hazards exist. Coming soon
Art. 1(13) Confirms the regulation does not affect the Euratom basic safety standards directive. Coming soon
Art. 1(14) Preserves Member States' right to restrict device use on matters outside this regulation. Coming soon
Art. 1(15) Preserves national law on organisation, delivery and financing of healthcare, including prescription requirements. Coming soon
Art. 1(16) Protects press freedom and freedom of expression in the media. Coming soon
Art. 2 DefinitionsIntroduces the definitions used in the regulation.
Art. 2(1) Defines medical device, including software, by its intended medical purposes and non-pharmacological action. Coming soon
Art. 2(2) Defines accessory as an article enabling or directly assisting a particular medical device's intended use. Coming soon
Art. 2(3) Defines custom-made device as made to a prescription for one specific patient. Coming soon
Art. 2(4) Defines active device as energy-dependent; software counts as active. Coming soon
Art. 2(5) Defines implantable device as one introduced into the body and left in place after the procedure. Coming soon
Art. 2(6) Defines invasive device as one penetrating the body through an orifice or surface. Coming soon
Art. 2(7) Defines generic device group by shared purpose or technology. Coming soon
Art. 2(8) Defines single-use device as intended for one patient in one procedure. Coming soon
Art. 2(9) Defines falsified device as one with false identity, source or certification presentation. Coming soon
Art. 2(10) Defines procedure pack as products packaged together for a specific medical purpose. Coming soon
Art. 2(11) Defines system as products intended to be interconnected for a medical purpose. Coming soon
Art. 2(12) Defines intended purpose from label, instructions, promotional materials and clinical evaluation. Coming soon
Art. 2(13) Defines label as written, printed or graphic information on device or packaging. Coming soon
Art. 2(14) Defines instructions for use as manufacturer information on purpose, proper use and precautions. Coming soon
Art. 2(15) Defines Unique Device Identifier as a standards-based code uniquely identifying devices. Coming soon
Art. 2(16) Defines non-viable as lacking metabolic or multiplication potential. Coming soon
Art. 2(17) Defines derivative as a cell-free substance extracted from human or animal tissue. Coming soon
Art. 2(18) Defines nanomaterial by particle size distribution in the 1-100 nm range. Coming soon
Art. 2(19) Defines particle for nanomaterial purposes as a small piece of matter with boundaries. Coming soon
Art. 2(20) Defines agglomerate as weakly bound particles with similar overall surface area. Coming soon
Art. 2(21) Defines aggregate as a particle of strongly bound or fused particles. Coming soon
Art. 2(22) Defines performance as the device's ability to achieve its stated intended purpose. Coming soon
Art. 2(23) Defines risk as probability of harm combined with its severity. Coming soon
Art. 2(24) Defines benefit-risk determination as analysis of all benefit and risk assessments for intended use. Coming soon
Art. 2(25) Defines compatibility of a device, including software, when used with other devices.
Art. 2(25)(a) Compatibility means performing as intended without loss when combined. Coming soon
Art. 2(25)(b) Compatibility means integrating or operating without modifying any combined part. Coming soon
Art. 2(25)(c) Compatibility means usable together without conflict, interference or adverse reaction. Coming soon
Art. 2(26) Defines interoperability among devices and software from the same or different manufacturers.
Art. 2(26)(a) Interoperability means exchanging and using information without altering data content. Coming soon
Art. 2(26)(b) Interoperability includes the ability to communicate with each other. Coming soon
Art. 2(26)(c) Interoperability includes working together as intended. Coming soon
Art. 2(27) Defines making available on the market as commercial supply, paid or free. Coming soon
Art. 2(28) Defines placing on the market as the first making available on the Union market. Coming soon
Art. 2(29) Defines putting into service as first availability to the final user, ready for use. Coming soon
Art. 2(30) Defines manufacturer as who makes or has made a device and markets it under own name. Coming soon
Art. 2(31) Defines full refurbishing as complete rebuilding with a new lifetime assigned. Coming soon
Art. 2(32) Defines authorised representative as an EU-established party mandated by a non-EU manufacturer. Coming soon
Art. 2(33) Defines importer as an EU party placing a third-country device on the market. Coming soon
Art. 2(34) Defines distributor as a supply-chain party, other than manufacturer or importer, making devices available. Coming soon
Art. 2(35) Defines economic operator as manufacturer, representative, importer, distributor or Article 22 person. Coming soon
Art. 2(36) Defines health institution as an organisation focused on patient care or public health. Coming soon
Art. 2(37) Defines user as any healthcare professional or lay person using a device. Coming soon
Art. 2(38) Defines lay person as someone without formal healthcare education. Coming soon
Art. 2(39) Defines reprocessing as processing a used device to enable safe reuse. Coming soon
Art. 2(40) Defines conformity assessment as demonstrating that regulatory requirements are fulfilled. Coming soon
Art. 2(41) Defines conformity assessment body as a third-party testing, certification or inspection body. Coming soon
Art. 2(42) Defines notified body as a designated conformity assessment body. Coming soon
Art. 2(43) Defines CE marking as the manufacturer's indication of conformity with applicable requirements. Coming soon
Art. 2(44) Defines clinical evaluation as a planned, continuous process assessing clinical data on safety and performance. Coming soon
Art. 2(45) Defines clinical investigation as systematic human-subject study assessing device safety or performance. Coming soon
Art. 2(46) Defines investigational device as one assessed in a clinical investigation. Coming soon
Art. 2(47) Defines clinical investigation plan as the document describing the study's design and conduct. Coming soon
Art. 2(48) Defines clinical data and its permitted sources. Coming soon
Art. 2(49) Defines sponsor as the party responsible for initiating, managing and financing an investigation. Coming soon
Art. 2(50) Defines subject as an individual participating in a clinical investigation. Coming soon
Art. 2(51) Defines clinical evidence as sufficient clinical data and evaluation results to assess safety and benefit. Coming soon
Art. 2(52) Defines clinical performance as achieving intended purpose with resulting patient benefit. Coming soon
Art. 2(53) Defines clinical benefit as positive, measurable patient-relevant health impact. Coming soon
Art. 2(54) Defines investigator as the person responsible for conduct at an investigation site. Coming soon
Art. 2(55) Defines informed consent as free, informed willingness to take part in an investigation. Coming soon
Art. 2(56) Defines ethics committee as an independent body empowered to give opinions. Coming soon
Art. 2(57) Defines adverse event in a clinical investigation as any untoward medical occurrence. Coming soon
Art. 2(58) Defines serious adverse event by listed grave outcomes.
Art. 2(58)(a) Serious adverse event includes one that led to death. Coming soon
Art. 2(58)(b) Serious adverse event includes serious health deterioration with listed consequences.
Art. 2(58)(b)(i) Deterioration resulting in life-threatening illness or injury. Coming soon
Art. 2(58)(b)(ii) Deterioration resulting in permanent impairment of body structure or function. Coming soon
Art. 2(58)(b)(iii) Deterioration resulting in hospitalisation or longer hospital stay. Coming soon
Art. 2(58)(b)(iv) Deterioration requiring intervention to prevent life-threatening harm or permanent impairment. Coming soon
Art. 2(58)(b)(v) Deterioration resulting in chronic disease. Coming soon
Art. 2(58)(c) Serious adverse event includes foetal distress, death, or congenital impairment. Coming soon
Art. 2(59) Defines device deficiency as any inadequacy of an investigational device or its information. Coming soon
Art. 2(60) Defines post-market surveillance as systematic proactive collection of experience from marketed devices. Coming soon
Art. 2(61) Defines market surveillance as authority activities checking device compliance and safety. Coming soon
Art. 2(62) Defines recall as measures to return devices already with end users. Coming soon
Art. 2(63) Defines withdrawal as measures stopping a device in the supply chain being made available. Coming soon
Art. 2(64) Defines incident as malfunction, deterioration, use-error, information inadequacy or undesirable side-effect. Coming soon
Art. 2(65) Defines serious incident by outcomes it caused or might cause.
Art. 2(65)(a) Serious incident includes one leading to death of a patient, user or other person. Coming soon
Art. 2(65)(b) Serious incident includes temporary or permanent serious health deterioration. Coming soon
Art. 2(65)(c) Serious incident includes one constituting a serious public health threat. Coming soon
Art. 2(66) Defines serious public health threat as an event risking death, serious harm or illness. Coming soon
Art. 2(67) Defines corrective action as action eliminating the cause of non-conformity. Coming soon
Art. 2(68) Defines field safety corrective action as manufacturer action reducing serious incident risk on the market. Coming soon
Art. 2(69) Defines field safety notice as a manufacturer communication about a corrective action. Coming soon
Art. 2(70) Defines harmonised standard as a European standard under the standardisation regulation. Coming soon
Art. 2(71) Defines common specifications as non-standard technical or clinical requirements providing a route to compliance. Coming soon
Art. 3 Amendment of certain definitionsEmpowers the Commission to amend nanomaterial definitions by delegated acts. Coming soon
Art. 4 Regulatory status of products
Art. 4(1) Commission determines by implementing act whether a product is a medical device or accessory. Coming soon
Art. 4(2) Commission may decide product status questions on its own initiative after consulting MDCG. Coming soon
Art. 4(3) Commission ensures Member States share expertise to determine products' regulatory status. Coming soon
Art. 4(4) Commission must consult EMA, ECHA and EFSA as relevant when deciding borderline product status. Coming soon
Art. 5 Placing on the market and putting into service
Art. 5(1) A device may be marketed only if compliant when supplied, installed, maintained and used as intended. Coming soon
Art. 5(2) Devices must satisfy applicable Annex I safety and performance requirements given their intended purpose. Coming soon
Art. 5(3) Proving conformity with safety and performance requirements must involve a clinical evaluation under Article 61. Coming soon
Art. 5(4) Devices made and used inside health institutions count as put into service. Coming soon
Art. 5(5) In-house hospital devices are exempt from most rules if listed conditions hold; states may restrict them.
Art. 5(5)(a) In-house devices must not be passed on to a different legal entity. Coming soon
Art. 5(5)(b) In-house devices must be made and used under suitable quality management systems. Coming soon
Art. 5(5)(c) Institution must document why patients' needs cannot be met by an equivalent marketed device. Coming soon
Art. 5(5)(d) Institution supplies its authority, on request, information and justification about making, changing and using such devices. Coming soon
Art. 5(5)(e) Institution must publish a declaration about the in-house devices and its own details.
Art. 5(5)(e)(i) Public declaration must give the manufacturing institution's name and address. Coming soon
Art. 5(5)(e)(ii) Public declaration must include details identifying the devices. Coming soon
Art. 5(5)(e)(iii) Declaration states devices meet Annex I requirements, noting and justifying any unmet ones. Coming soon
Art. 5(5)(f) Institution keeps documentation on facility, process, design and performance sufficient for authority verification. Coming soon
Art. 5(5)(g) Institution must ensure every device is made according to its documentation. Coming soon
Art. 5(5)(h) Institution reviews clinical-use experience and takes needed corrective action. Coming soon
Art. 5(6) Commission may adopt implementing acts to harmonise interpretation and application of Annex I. Coming soon
Art. 6 Distance sales
Art. 6(1) Devices offered online to people in the Union must comply with the Regulation. Coming soon
Art. 6(2) Devices used to provide remote diagnostic or therapeutic services in the Union must comply too. Coming soon
Art. 6(3) On authority request, sellers or service providers must supply the EU declaration of conformity. Coming soon
Art. 6(4) Member States may require online service providers to stop activity to protect public health. Coming soon
Art. 7 ClaimsLabelling, instructions, advertising and similar material must not mislead about purpose, safety or performance.
Art. 7(a) Must not claim functions or properties the device lacks. Coming soon
Art. 7(b) Must not give a false impression of treatment, diagnosis or capabilities. Coming soon
Art. 7(c) Must not hide a likely risk from intended-purpose use. Coming soon
Art. 7(d) Must not suggest uses beyond the intended purpose that was assessed. Coming soon
Art. 8 Use of harmonised standards
Art. 8(1) Conformity with published harmonised standards creates a presumption of conformity with the covered requirements. Coming soon
Art. 8(2) Harmonised standards references also cover published European Pharmacopoeia monographs. Coming soon
Art. 9 Common specifications
Art. 9(1) Commission may adopt common specifications where standards are missing or insufficient. Coming soon
Art. 9(2) Devices meeting common specifications are presumed conforming to the covered requirements. Coming soon
Art. 9(3) Manufacturers must follow common specifications unless justifying an equally safe alternative. Coming soon
Art. 9(4) Makers of Annex XVI products must comply with the relevant common specifications without exception. Coming soon
Art. 10 General obligations of manufacturers
Art. 10(1) Manufacturers must design and make devices in accordance with the Regulation. Coming soon
Art. 10(2) Manufacturers must set up, document and maintain a risk management system. Coming soon
Art. 10(3) Manufacturers must perform clinical evaluation, including post-market clinical follow-up. Coming soon
Art. 10(4) Manufacturers must draw up and update technical documentation per Annexes II and III. Coming soon
Art. 10(5) Custom-made device makers must keep documentation available to authorities per Annex XIII. Coming soon
Art. 10(6) After conformity assessment, manufacturers issue an EU declaration of conformity and affix CE marking. Coming soon
Art. 10(7) Manufacturers must meet unique device identification and registration obligations. Coming soon
Art. 10(8) Keep technical documentation and declaration available to authorities for ten years, fifteen for implants. Coming soon
Art. 10(9) Manufacturers must maintain procedures for series conformity and a quality management system covering listed aspects.
Art. 10(9)(a) Quality system covers regulatory compliance strategy and modification management. Coming soon
Art. 10(9)(b) Quality system identifies applicable safety and performance requirements and ways to meet them. Coming soon
Art. 10(9)(c) Quality system addresses management responsibility. Coming soon
Art. 10(9)(d) Quality system covers resource management, including supplier and subcontractor control. Coming soon
Art. 10(9)(e) Quality system includes risk management per Annex I Section 3. Coming soon
Art. 10(9)(f) Quality system includes clinical evaluation and post-market clinical follow-up. Coming soon
Art. 10(9)(g) Quality system covers product realisation from planning through design, production and service. Coming soon
Art. 10(9)(h) Quality system verifies UDI assignments and consistency of registered information. Coming soon
Art. 10(9)(i) Quality system includes setting up and maintaining post-market surveillance. Coming soon
Art. 10(9)(j) Quality system handles communication with authorities, notified bodies, operators and customers. Coming soon
Art. 10(9)(k) Quality system has processes for reporting serious incidents and field corrective actions. Coming soon
Art. 10(9)(l) Quality system manages corrective and preventive actions and checks their effectiveness. Coming soon
Art. 10(9)(m) Quality system includes monitoring, measurement, data analysis and product improvement processes. Coming soon
Art. 10(10) Manufacturers must implement and update the post-market surveillance system. Coming soon
Art. 10(11) Devices ship with required information in official languages; labels indelible and legible. Coming soon
Art. 10(12) Manufacturers must promptly correct, withdraw or recall nonconforming devices and notify relevant parties. Coming soon
Art. 10(13) Manufacturers need a system for recording and reporting incidents and field safety actions. Coming soon
Art. 10(14) Manufacturers must give authorities requested conformity information, samples, and cooperation on corrective action. Coming soon
Art. 10(15) Identity of any external designer or manufacturer must be included in registration information. Coming soon
Art. 10(16) Manufacturers must have proportionate financial cover for potential liability for defective devices. Coming soon
Art. 10a Obligations in case of interruption or discontinuation of supply of certain devices
Art. 10a(1) Manufacturers must give six months' notice of supply interruptions risking serious harm. Coming soon
Art. 10a(2) Receiving authority informs other Member States' authorities and the Commission of the interruption. Coming soon
Art. 10a(3) Operators receiving supply interruption notice must pass it on down the chain. Coming soon
Art. 11 Authorised representative
Art. 11(1) Non-EU manufacturers must designate a sole authorised representative to place devices on the market. Coming soon
Art. 11(2) Designation is a mandate valid only when accepted in writing. Coming soon
Art. 11(3) Authorised representative performs mandate tasks, which manufacturer must enable, as listed.
Art. 11(3)(a) Representative verifies declaration, technical documentation and conformity assessment were completed. Coming soon
Art. 11(3)(b) Representative keeps documentation copies available to authorities for the required period. Coming soon
Art. 11(3)(c) Representative complies with registration duties and checks manufacturer's UDI and registration compliance. Coming soon
Art. 11(3)(d) Representative gives authorities requested conformity information in the required language. Coming soon
Art. 11(3)(e) Representative forwards sample requests to manufacturer and ensures authority gets samples or access. Coming soon
Art. 11(3)(f) Representative cooperates with authorities on preventive or corrective actions. Coming soon
Art. 11(3)(g) Representative promptly passes suspected incident complaints to the manufacturer. Coming soon
Art. 11(3)(h) Representative ends the mandate if the manufacturer breaches its obligations. Coming soon
Art. 11(4) Manufacturer's core obligations listed cannot be delegated through the mandate. Coming soon
Art. 11(5) Representative is jointly liable for defective devices when non-EU manufacturer breaches Article 10. Coming soon
Art. 11(6) Representative ending mandate must promptly tell authority and notified body with reasons. Coming soon
Art. 11(7) References to manufacturer's authority mean the representative's Member State authority. Coming soon
Art. 12 Change of authorised representativeChanging authorised representative requires an agreement covering specified transition aspects.
Art. 12(a) Agreement sets mandate end and start dates. Coming soon
Art. 12(b) Agreement sets last date outgoing representative may appear in manufacturer information. Coming soon
Art. 12(c) Agreement covers document transfer, confidentiality and property rights. Coming soon
Art. 12(d) Outgoing representative must forward later incident complaints to manufacturer or successor. Coming soon
Art. 13 General obligations of importers
Art. 13(1) Importers may place only conforming devices on the Union market. Coming soon
Art. 13(2) Importers verify conformity points before placing devices and report nonconformity or serious risk.
Art. 13(2)(a) Importer checks CE marking and that declaration of conformity exists. Coming soon
Art. 13(2)(b) Importer checks manufacturer is identified and an authorised representative designated. Coming soon
Art. 13(2)(c) Importer checks labelling and instructions for use are present as required. Coming soon
Art. 13(2)(d) Importer checks a UDI was assigned where applicable. Coming soon
Art. 13(3) Importers show their name and address on device or packaging without obscuring manufacturer labels. Coming soon
Art. 13(4) Importers verify device registration and add their own details. Coming soon
Art. 13(5) Importers must keep storage and transport conditions that preserve device compliance. Coming soon
Art. 13(6) Importers keep a register of complaints, nonconforming devices, recalls and withdrawals. Coming soon
Art. 13(7) Importers must report nonconformity to manufacturer and authorities and cooperate on corrective action. Coming soon
Art. 13(8) Importers must promptly forward incident complaints to manufacturer and its representative. Coming soon
Art. 13(9) Importers retain copies of declaration of conformity and certificates for the required period. Coming soon
Art. 13(10) Importers cooperate with authorities and provide free samples or access on request. Coming soon
Art. 14 General obligations of distributors
Art. 14(1) Distributors must act with due care regarding applicable requirements. Coming soon
Art. 14(2) Distributors verify conformity points before supply and report nonconforming or seriously risky devices.
Art. 14(2)(a) Distributor checks CE marking and that declaration of conformity exists. Coming soon
Art. 14(2)(b) Distributor checks device comes with manufacturer's required information. Coming soon
Art. 14(2)(c) Distributor checks importer met its name-and-address labelling duty. Coming soon
Art. 14(2)(d) Distributor checks a UDI was assigned where applicable. Coming soon
Art. 14(3) Distributors keep storage and transport within manufacturer's conditions. Coming soon
Art. 14(4) Distributors must inform and cooperate on corrective action for nonconforming or risky devices. Coming soon
Art. 14(5) Distributors forward incident complaints and maintain a register of complaints and recalls. Coming soon
Art. 14(6) Distributors give authorities information, cooperation and free samples on request. Coming soon
Art. 15 Person responsible for regulatory compliance
Art. 15(1) Manufacturers need a regulatory compliance person with qualifying expertise or experience.
Art. 15(1)(a) Qualification route: relevant degree plus one year regulatory or quality experience. Coming soon
Art. 15(1)(b) Qualification route: four years of regulatory or quality management experience. Coming soon
Art. 15(2) Micro and small enterprises must have such a person permanently available, not necessarily employed. Coming soon
Art. 15(3) Compliance person is responsible for ensuring the listed duties are met.
Art. 15(3)(a) Compliance person ensures conformity is checked before each device is released. Coming soon
Art. 15(3)(b) Compliance person ensures technical documentation and declaration are drawn up and current. Coming soon
Art. 15(3)(c) Compliance person ensures post-market surveillance obligations are met. Coming soon
Art. 15(3)(d) Compliance person ensures incident and vigilance reporting duties are fulfilled. Coming soon
Art. 15(3)(e) For investigational devices, compliance person issues the required statement. Coming soon
Art. 15(4) Where several people share compliance duties, their responsibilities must be written down. Coming soon
Art. 15(5) Compliance person must not be disadvantaged for properly performing their duties. Coming soon
Art. 15(6) Authorised representatives need a compliance person with required expertise permanently available.
Art. 15(6)(a) Compliance officer may qualify through a relevant degree plus one year's regulatory or quality experience. Coming soon
Art. 15(6)(b) Alternatively, four years' professional experience in regulatory or quality work for devices suffices. Coming soon
Art. 16 Cases in which obligations of manufacturers apply to importers, distributors or other persons
Art. 16(1) Distributors, importers or others take on manufacturer duties in certain situations; individual-patient adaptation is excluded.
Art. 16(1)(a) Marketing a device under one's own name makes one the manufacturer, unless an agreement names the manufacturer. Coming soon
Art. 16(1)(b) Changing the intended purpose of a device already on the market creates manufacturer obligations. Coming soon
Art. 16(1)(c) Modifying a marketed device so compliance may be affected creates manufacturer obligations. Coming soon
Art. 16(2) Introduces activities that do not count as compliance-affecting modifications of a device.
Art. 16(2)(a) Providing or translating manufacturer information needed for a Member State is not a modification. Coming soon
Art. 16(2)(b) Outer repackaging needed for a market is not a modification if device condition is unaffected. Coming soon
Art. 16(3) Relabelling or repackaging parties must mark their details and run a quality system covering translation and packaging. Coming soon
Art. 16(4) Relabellers and repackagers must notify manufacturer and authority 28 days ahead and submit a notified-body certificate. Coming soon
Art. 17 Single-use devices and their reprocessing
Art. 17(1) Single-use device reprocessing is allowed only if national law permits and this Article is followed. Coming soon
Art. 17(2) Whoever reprocesses a single-use device becomes its manufacturer, with traceability duties and producer liability. Coming soon
Art. 17(3) Member States may relax manufacturer rules for in-hospital reprocessing if safeguards hold; patient information encouraged.
Art. 17(3)(a) Reprocessed device must be as safe and performant as the original and meet listed Article 5(5) conditions. Coming soon
Art. 17(3)(b) Reprocessing must follow common specifications on risk, validation, release, quality, incident reporting and traceability. Coming soon
Art. 17(4) Member States may extend the hospital derogation to external reprocessors returning the whole device to the hospital. Coming soon
Art. 17(5) Commission adopts reprocessing common specifications; otherwise standards apply, and a notified body certifies compliance. Coming soon
Art. 17(6) Only single-use devices lawfully placed on the market may be reprocessed. Coming soon
Art. 17(7) Reprocessing must be safe according to current scientific evidence. Coming soon
Art. 17(8) Reprocessed device labels show the reprocessor's details; original manufacturer moves to instructions for use. Coming soon
Art. 17(9) Member States may impose stricter national limits on reprocessing and must notify the Commission.
Art. 17(9)(a) National rules may restrict reprocessing or transferring single-use devices elsewhere for reprocessing. Coming soon
Art. 17(9)(b) National rules may restrict supplying or further using reprocessed single-use devices. Coming soon
Art. 17(10) Commission must report on this Article's operation by May 2024 and propose amendments if needed. Coming soon
Art. 18 Implant card and information to be supplied to the patient with an implanted device
Art. 18(1) Implant manufacturers must supply patient information and an implant card, in lay language, kept updated online.
Art. 18(1)(a) Implant information must identify the device: name, serial, lot, UDI, model and manufacturer details. Coming soon
Art. 18(1)(b) Provide warnings and precautions about interference from external influences, examinations or environments. Coming soon
Art. 18(1)(c) Provide expected device lifetime and any required follow-up. Coming soon
Art. 18(1)(d) Provide any other information needed for the patient to use the implant safely. Coming soon
Art. 18(2) Member States make health institutions give implanted patients the information and a named implant card. Coming soon
Art. 18(3) Listed minor implants such as sutures and screws are exempt; Commission may amend the list. Coming soon
Art. 19 EU declaration of conformity
Art. 19(1) EU declaration of conformity must state compliance, follow Annex IV, be kept current and translated. Coming soon
Art. 19(2) Where other Union laws require a declaration, issue one single declaration covering all of them. Coming soon
Art. 19(3) Issuing the declaration makes the manufacturer responsible for compliance with this and other applicable Union law. Coming soon
Art. 19(4) Commission may amend the declaration's minimum content through delegated acts. Coming soon
Art. 20 CE marking of conformity
Art. 20(1) Conforming devices, except custom-made or investigational ones, must carry the CE marking. Coming soon
Art. 20(2) CE marking follows the general principles of Regulation 765/2008. Coming soon
Art. 20(3) CE marking must be visible, legible, indelible on device or packaging, and appear in instructions. Coming soon
Art. 20(4) Affix CE marking before market placement; a risk or use pictogram may follow. Coming soon
Art. 20(5) Notified body identification number follows the CE marking and appears in related promotional material. Coming soon
Art. 20(6) CE marking also signals conformity with any other Union legislation requiring it. Coming soon
Art. 21 Devices for special purposes
Art. 21(1) Member States must not obstruct investigational or custom-made devices; these do not bear CE marking.
Art. 21(1)(a) No obstacles to investigational devices supplied to investigators under the clinical investigation rules. Coming soon
Art. 21(1)(b) No obstacles to custom-made devices meeting Article 52(8) and Annex XIII. Coming soon
Art. 21(2) Custom-made devices need the Annex XIII statement for the identified patient; states may request lists. Coming soon
Art. 21(3) Non-compliant devices may be shown at fairs if clearly signed as demonstration only. Coming soon
Art. 22 Systems and procedure packs
Art. 22(1) Anyone combining CE-marked devices with other products into a system or pack must draw up a statement.
Art. 22(1)(a) Combinations may include other CE-marked devices. Coming soon
Art. 22(1)(b) Combinations may include CE-marked in vitro diagnostic devices under Regulation 2017/746. Coming soon
Art. 22(1)(c) Combinations may include other lawful products when used in a medical procedure or justified. Coming soon
Art. 22(2) The pack statement must contain specified declarations.
Art. 22(2)(a) Declare that compatibility was verified and work followed the manufacturers' instructions. Coming soon
Art. 22(2)(b) Declare that the pack was packaged and users received the component manufacturers' information. Coming soon
Art. 22(2)(c) Declare that combining was subject to internal monitoring, verification and validation. Coming soon
Art. 22(3) Sterilising systems or packs requires an Annex IX or XI procedure and a sterilisation statement. Coming soon
Art. 22(4) Packs with non-CE devices, incompatible combinations or improper sterilisation are treated as devices needing conformity assessment. Coming soon
Art. 22(5) Packs carry no extra CE marking but show assembler's details; statement retained for authorities. Coming soon
Art. 23 Parts and components
Art. 23(1) Suppliers of replacement parts must ensure safety and performance are unaffected and keep evidence. Coming soon
Art. 23(2) A replacement part significantly changing performance, safety or purpose counts as a device. Coming soon
Art. 24 Free movementMember States must not restrict market availability of devices that comply with the Regulation. Coming soon
Art. 25 Identification within the supply chain
Art. 25(1) Distributors and importers cooperate with manufacturers or representatives to ensure device traceability. Coming soon
Art. 25(2) Economic operators must be able to identify supply-chain parties to authorities for the retention period.
Art. 25(2)(a) Be able to identify any operator they directly supplied. Coming soon
Art. 25(2)(b) Be able to identify any operator that directly supplied them. Coming soon
Art. 25(2)(c) Be able to identify health institutions or professionals they directly supplied. Coming soon
Art. 26 Medical devices nomenclatureCommission provides an internationally recognised device nomenclature free of charge. Coming soon
Art. 27 Unique Device Identification system
Art. 27(1) The UDI system aids device identification and traceability, comprising defined components.
Art. 27(1)(a) The system produces a UDI made of defined identifiers.
Art. 27(1)(a)(i) UDI includes a device identifier specific to manufacturer and device, giving access to Annex VI data. Coming soon
Art. 27(1)(a)(ii) UDI includes a production identifier for the production unit and packaged devices. Coming soon
Art. 27(1)(b) UDI is placed on the device label or packaging. Coming soon
Art. 27(1)(c) Operators, institutions and professionals store UDIs under paragraphs 8 and 9. Coming soon
Art. 27(1)(d) A UDI database is established under Article 28. Coming soon
Art. 27(2) Commission designates UDI issuing entities meeting listed criteria and aims for universally readable carriers.
Art. 27(2)(a) Issuing entity must be an organisation with legal personality. Coming soon
Art. 27(2)(b) Its assignment system must adequately identify devices through distribution and use. Coming soon
Art. 27(2)(c) Its assignment system must conform to relevant international standards. Coming soon
Art. 27(2)(d) It must offer access to all interested users on transparent predetermined terms. Coming soon
Art. 27(2)(e) The entity must make specified undertakings.
Art. 27(2)(e)(i) Operate the assignment system for at least ten years after designation. Coming soon
Art. 27(2)(e)(ii) Give the Commission and Member States information about its system on request. Coming soon
Art. 27(2)(e)(iii) Stay compliant with designation criteria and terms. Coming soon
Art. 27(3) Before marketing, manufacturers assign UDIs to devices and packaging and submit Annex VI data to the database. Coming soon
Art. 27(4) UDI carriers go on device labels and all higher packaging levels, excluding shipping containers. Coming soon
Art. 27(5) UDI is used when reporting serious incidents and field safety corrective actions. Coming soon
Art. 27(6) Basic UDI-DI must appear on the EU declaration of conformity. Coming soon
Art. 27(7) Manufacturer keeps an up-to-date list of assigned UDIs in technical documentation. Coming soon
Art. 27(8) Economic operators keep UDIs of class III implantables and designated devices they supplied or received. Coming soon
Art. 27(9) Health institutions store UDIs of class III implantables; other storage encouraged or required by states. Coming soon
Art. 27(10) Commission may amend UDI provisions through delegated acts.
Art. 27(10)(a) Delegated acts may update the Annex VI Part B information list. Coming soon
Art. 27(10)(b) Delegated acts may amend Annex VI following international and technical developments. Coming soon
Art. 27(11) Commission may adopt implementing acts detailing UDI system arrangements.
Art. 27(11)(a) Implementing acts may determine which devices must have UDIs stored under paragraph 8. Coming soon
Art. 27(11)(b) Implementing acts may specify the data content of production identifiers. Coming soon
Art. 27(12) Commission must weigh listed considerations when adopting UDI measures.
Art. 27(12)(a) Consider confidentiality and data protection. Coming soon
Art. 27(12)(b) Consider the risk-based approach. Coming soon
Art. 27(12)(c) Consider cost-effectiveness. Coming soon
Art. 27(12)(d) Consider convergence with international UDI systems. Coming soon
Art. 27(12)(e) Consider avoiding duplication within the UDI system. Coming soon
Art. 27(12)(f) Consider healthcare system needs and compatibility with other identification systems. Coming soon
Art. 28 UDI database
Art. 28(1) Commission sets up and manages a public UDI database holding Annex VI Part B information. Coming soon
Art. 28(2) Database design follows Annex VI principles and must exclude production identifiers and confidential commercial data. Coming soon
Art. 28(3) Core UDI database data elements are publicly accessible free of charge. Coming soon
Art. 28(4) Database design maximises accessibility, including multi-user access and automatic transfers; Commission supports users. Coming soon
Art. 29 Registration of devices
Art. 29(1) Before marketing, manufacturers assign a Basic UDI-DI and submit it with core data to the database. Coming soon
Art. 29(2) Systems and procedure packs also need a Basic UDI-DI and core data submitted before marketing. Coming soon
Art. 29(3) For notified-body-assessed devices, assign Basic UDI-DI before applying; submit data after certification and before marketing. Coming soon
Art. 29(4) Before marketing, manufacturers enter or verify Eudamed device information and keep it updated. Coming soon
Art. 30 Electronic system for registration of economic operators
Art. 30(1) Commission builds an electronic system generating registration numbers and collecting operator identification information. Coming soon
Art. 30(2) Member States may have national registration rules for distributors. Coming soon
Art. 30(3) Importers verify within two weeks that operator information was submitted and add their own details. Coming soon
Art. 31 Registration of manufacturers, authorised representatives and importers
Art. 31(1) Manufacturers, representatives and importers register their Annex VI details before marketing and before notified-body applications. Coming soon
Art. 31(2) Competent authority verifies registration data and issues a single registration number. Coming soon
Art. 31(3) Manufacturer uses the registration number for notified-body applications and Eudamed access. Coming soon
Art. 31(4) Operators update registration data within one week of any change. Coming soon
Art. 31(5) Operators confirm data accuracy after one year and every two years; states may act on failure. Coming soon
Art. 31(6) Competent authority checks the registration data that economic operators have confirmed. Coming soon
Art. 31(7) Registration data entered in the electronic system must be publicly accessible. Coming soon
Art. 31(8) Authorities may use registration data to charge operators a fee. Coming soon
Art. 32 Summary of safety and clinical performance
Art. 32(1) Manufacturers of implantable and class III devices must produce a public, validated safety and clinical performance summary. Coming soon
Art. 32(2) Sets the minimum content areas the safety and clinical performance summary must cover.
Art. 32(2)(a) Summary must identify the device and manufacturer, with Basic UDI-DI and SRN if issued. Coming soon
Art. 32(2)(b) Summary must state intended purpose, indications, contraindications and target populations. Coming soon
Art. 32(2)(c) Summary must describe the device, earlier versions, differences and combined accessories or products. Coming soon
Art. 32(2)(d) Summary must list possible diagnostic or therapeutic alternatives. Coming soon
Art. 32(2)(e) Summary must cite harmonised standards and common specifications that were applied. Coming soon
Art. 32(2)(f) Summary must include the clinical evaluation summary and post-market clinical follow-up information. Coming soon
Art. 32(2)(g) Summary must propose a user profile and training. Coming soon
Art. 32(2)(h) Summary must give residual risks, undesirable effects, warnings and precautions. Coming soon
Art. 32(3) Commission may define by implementing act the format of summary data elements. Coming soon
Art. 33 European database on medical devices
Art. 33(1) Commission establishes and runs the Eudamed database for stated purposes.
Art. 33(1)(a) Eudamed informs the public about devices, certificates and economic operators. Coming soon
Art. 33(1)(b) Eudamed enables unique device identification and traceability in the internal market. Coming soon
Art. 33(1)(c) Eudamed informs public on clinical investigations and supports sponsor compliance. Coming soon
Art. 33(1)(d) Eudamed helps manufacturers meet vigilance and surveillance information obligations. Coming soon
Art. 33(1)(e) Eudamed supports authorities and Commission tasks and cooperation. Coming soon
Art. 33(2) Lists the electronic systems that Eudamed comprises.
Art. 33(2)(a) Eudamed includes the device registration system. Coming soon
Art. 33(2)(b) Eudamed includes the UDI database. Coming soon
Art. 33(2)(c) Eudamed includes the economic operator registration system. Coming soon
Art. 33(2)(d) Eudamed includes the system on notified bodies and certificates. Coming soon
Art. 33(2)(e) Eudamed includes the clinical investigations system. Coming soon
Art. 33(2)(f) Eudamed includes the vigilance and post-market surveillance system. Coming soon
Art. 33(2)(g) Eudamed includes the market surveillance system. Coming soon
Art. 33(3) Commission should design Eudamed to be compatible with national databases for data exchange. Coming soon
Art. 33(4) Member States, notified bodies, operators and sponsors enter data; Commission offers support. Coming soon
Art. 33(5) Eudamed information is accessible to various parties as specified; public parts must be user-friendly. Coming soon

Art. 33(7) Data subjects can exercise access, correction and erasure rights, with fixes within 60 days. Coming soon
Art. 33(8) Commission sets detailed Eudamed arrangements and avoids duplicate data entry. Coming soon

Art. 34(3) Commission publishes an Official Journal notice once Eudamed conditions are met. Coming soon

Art. 35(8) Notified-body authority takes part in peer review activities. Coming soon

Art. 37(3) Notified bodies publish a list of their subsidiaries. Coming soon

Art. 37(5) Notified bodies keep subcontractor qualification and work records available to the authority. Coming soon

Art. 38(1) Conformity assessment bodies apply for designation to their responsible authority. Coming soon
Art. 38(2) Application states activities and device types, with documentation showing Annex VII compliance. Coming soon
Art. 38(3) Notified body keeps its application documentation updated when changes occur. Coming soon
Art. 39 Assessment of the application
Art. 39(1) Authority checks application completeness within 30 days and drafts a preliminary assessment report. Coming soon
Art. 39(2) Preliminary assessment report goes to the Commission, which passes it to MDCG. Coming soon
Art. 39(3) Commission and MDCG appoint a joint assessment team within 14 days. Coming soon
Art. 39(4) Joint team reviews documents within 90 days and joins an on-site assessment. Coming soon
Art. 39(5) Non-compliances are discussed, listed, and the applicant submits a corrective action plan. Coming soon
Art. 39(6) Joint team documents remaining diverging opinions within 30 days of on-site assessment. Coming soon
Art. 39(7) Authority evaluates the corrective plan, consults the joint team and drafts the final report. Coming soon
Art. 39(8) Authority submits final assessment report and draft designation to Commission, MDCG and team. Coming soon
Art. 39(9) Joint team gives final opinion in 21 days; MDCG recommends within 42 days. Coming soon
Art. 39(10) Commission may set detailed procedures and reports for designation applications by implementing act. Coming soon
Art. 40 Nomination of experts for joint assessment of applications for notification
Art. 40(1) Member States and Commission nominate qualified experts for assessing conformity assessment bodies. Coming soon
Art. 40(2) Commission maintains and shares a list of nominated experts. Coming soon
Art. 41 Language requirementsDesignation documents use a language set by the Member State; Commission provides translations. Coming soon
Art. 42 Designation and notification procedure
Art. 42(1) Member States may designate only bodies that completed assessment and meet Annex VII. Coming soon
Art. 42(2) Member States notify designated bodies to Commission and others through NANDO. Coming soon
Art. 42(3) Notification must specify designation scope using codes, and any conditions. Coming soon
Art. 42(4) Notification includes assessment report, team opinion and MDCG recommendation, with justification if departed from. Coming soon
Art. 42(5) Notifying state reports conditions and evidence of ongoing monitoring arrangements. Coming soon
Art. 42(6) Objections may be raised within 28 days; otherwise notification is published within 42 days. Coming soon
Art. 42(7) If objections arise, MDCG gives opinion within 40 days and publication follows. Coming soon
Art. 42(8) Notifying state responds in writing to a confirmed MDCG objection within 40 days. Coming soon
Art. 42(9) If designation is upheld, Commission publishes the notification within 14 days. Coming soon
Art. 42(10) On publication, Commission adds notification documents and responses to the certificates system. Coming soon
Art. 42(11) Designation is valid from the day after NANDO publication and states scope. Coming soon
Art. 42(12) A body may act as notified body only once designation is valid. Coming soon
Art. 42(13) Commission lists codes for device types to define designation scope. Coming soon
Art. 43 Identification number and list of notified bodies
Art. 43(1) Commission assigns each notified body a single identification number. Coming soon
Art. 43(2) Commission publishes and keeps current the public list of notified bodies. Coming soon
Art. 44 Monitoring and re-assessment of notified bodies
Art. 44(1) Notified bodies report relevant compliance-affecting changes to their authority within 15 days. Coming soon
Art. 44(2) Authorities monitor notified bodies; bodies supply requested information to verify compliance. Coming soon
Art. 44(3) Requests to notified bodies from other states are copied to its authority; response within 15 days. Coming soon
Art. 44(4) Authorities re-assess notified bodies annually with on-site audit under an annual plan. Coming soon
Art. 44(5) Monitoring includes observed audits of notified body staff at manufacturer assessments. Coming soon
Art. 44(6) Monitoring uses surveillance data and systematically follows up complaints about notified bodies. Coming soon
Art. 44(7) Authority may conduct short-notice, unannounced or for-cause reviews. Coming soon
Art. 44(8) Authority reviews notified body assessments of technical and clinical documentation. Coming soon
Art. 44(9) Authority records non-compliance findings and tracks corrective actions. Coming soon
Art. 44(10) Complete re-assessment of notified bodies occurs every five years with a joint team. Coming soon
Art. 44(11) Commission may amend re-assessment frequency through delegated acts. Coming soon
Art. 44(12) Member States report yearly on notified body monitoring, with a public summary. Coming soon

Art. 45(1) Authority reviews a suitable number of notified body technical and clinical documentation assessments. Coming soon
Art. 45(2) File sampling must be planned, representative, risk-based, justified and documented. Coming soon
Art. 45(3) Authority checks notified body procedures and conclusions, using common specifications. Coming soon
Art. 45(4) These reviews form part of re-assessment and joint assessments, using suitable expertise. Coming soon
Art. 45(5) MDCG may recommend adjusting sampling proportion based on reports and surveillance input. Coming soon
Art. 45(6) Commission may adopt implementing acts on documentation review arrangements. Coming soon

Art. 46(2) Commission publishes amended notification in NANDO and records changes in the electronic system. Coming soon

Art. 46(6) Authority ensures files of affected notified body are kept and shared on request. Coming soon

Art. 46(7)(b) Authority reports findings to Commission and states within three months. Coming soon
Art. 46(7)(c) Authority requires notified body to suspend or withdraw unduly issued certificates. Coming soon
Art. 46(7)(d) Authority records suspended or withdrawn certificates in the electronic system. Coming soon
Art. 46(7)(e) Authority informs manufacturer's national competent authority of certificate suspensions, which acts against risks. Coming soon

Art. 46(8)(b) Certificates stay valid if none issued during suspension; manufacturer may need substitute body confirmation. Coming soon

Art. 46(9)(a) Competent authority confirms no safety issue with the devices concerned. Coming soon
Art. 46(9)(b) Another notified body confirms in writing it takes responsibility and finishes assessment within twelve months. Coming soon

Art. 47(2) Notifying state gives Commission requested information about the body's designation. Coming soon
Art. 47(3) Commission may start reassessment or on-site expert participation where competence concerns persist. Coming soon

Art. 47(5) Commission must treat confidential information from investigations confidentially. Coming soon
Art. 48 Peer review and exchange of experience between authorities responsible for notified bodies
Art. 48(1) Commission organises exchange of experience between authorities responsible for notified bodies.
Art. 48(1)(a) Exchange covers developing best practice documents for authorities. Coming soon
Art. 48(1)(b) Exchange covers guidance documents for notified bodies on implementing the Regulation. Coming soon
Art. 48(1)(c) Exchange covers training and qualification of assessment experts. Coming soon
Art. 48(1)(d) Exchange covers monitoring trends in designation changes, certificate withdrawals and transfers. Coming soon
Art. 48(1)(e) Exchange covers monitoring use and applicability of scope codes. Coming soon
Art. 48(1)(f) Exchange covers building a peer review mechanism for authorities and Commission. Coming soon
Art. 48(1)(g) Exchange covers ways to inform the public about oversight of notified bodies. Coming soon
Art. 48(2) Authorities take part in peer review every third year. Coming soon
Art. 48(3) Commission helps organise and support the peer review mechanism. Coming soon
Art. 48(4) Commission publishes an annual summary report of peer review activities. Coming soon
Art. 48(5) Commission may adopt implementing acts detailing peer review and training arrangements. Coming soon
Art. 49 Coordination of notified bodiesCommission ensures a notified body coordination group meets at least annually. Coming soon
Art. 50 List of standard feesNotified bodies publish lists of their standard conformity assessment fees. Coming soon
Art. 51 Classification of devices
Art. 51(1) Devices are classed I, IIa, IIb or III by intended purpose and risk per Annex VIII. Coming soon
Art. 51(2) Classification disputes between manufacturer and notified body go to the competent authority. Coming soon
Art. 51(3) Commission decides on classification application or reclassification at a Member State's request.
Art. 51(3)(a) Commission decides how Annex VIII applies to a device or group. Coming soon
Art. 51(3)(b) Commission may reclassify devices for public health reasons based on new evidence. Coming soon

Art. 52(14)(b) Implementing acts may set minimum frequency of unannounced audits and sample tests. Coming soon
Art. 52(14)(c) Implementing acts may specify tests notified bodies carry out during assessments. Coming soon

Art. 57(1)(c) System holds notification information and amended notifications. Coming soon
Art. 57(1)(d) System holds the list of notified bodies. Coming soon

Art. 57(1)(h) System holds the certificate information entered by notified bodies. Coming soon

Art. 62 General requirements regarding clinical investigations conducted to demonstrate conformity of devices

Art. 62(1)(b) Purpose: establish and verify the clinical benefits the manufacturer specifies. Coming soon
Art. 62(1)(c) Purpose: verify clinical safety, identify side-effects and judge risk acceptability against benefits. Coming soon

Art. 62(4)(b) Ethics committee must not have issued a negative opinion. Coming soon
Art. 62(4)(c) Sponsor, legal representative or contact person must be established in the Union. Coming soon
Art. 62(4)(d) Vulnerable populations and subjects must be appropriately protected. Coming soon

Art. 62(4)(m) Annex XV requirements must be fulfilled. Coming soon

Art. 62(6) Investigators and staff must have appropriate qualifications, knowledge and experience. Coming soon
Art. 62(7) Investigation facilities must be suitable and resemble intended use facilities. Coming soon

Art. 63(2)(a)(ii) Subject must understand protection rights, including refusing or withdrawing without detriment. Coming soon

Art. 63(2)(b) Information must be comprehensive, concise, clear, relevant and understandable. Coming soon
Art. 63(2)(c) Information must be given in a prior interview with a qualified team member. Coming soon
Art. 63(2)(d) Information must cover the applicable damage compensation system. Coming soon
Art. 63(2)(e) Information must include the EU-wide investigation identification number and results availability. Coming soon

Art. 65(e) Investigation must target minor-only conditions or be essential for validating data from adults. Coming soon

Art. 68(1)(b) Scientific grounds expect direct, clinically relevant, measurable benefit to the subject. Coming soon

Art. 93(11) Authorities cooperate with third-country authorities on information exchange and surveillance support. Coming soon
