Art. 94(a) Trigger: device may present unacceptable risk to health, safety or public health. Coming soon
Art. 94(b) Trigger: device otherwise fails requirements of the Regulation. Coming soon
Art. 95 Procedure for dealing with devices presenting an unacceptable risk to health and safety
Art. 95(1) Authorities require operators to take corrective action, restrict, withdraw or recall risky devices. Coming soon
Art. 95(2) Authorities notify the Commission, states and notified body of evaluation results and required actions. Coming soon
Art. 95(3) Operators must ensure corrective action is taken across the Union for all concerned devices. Coming soon
Art. 95(4) If operators fail to act, authorities restrict or recall the device and notify others. Coming soon
Art. 95(5) Notification of national measures must include identification, origin, non-compliance reasons, risk and measure details. Coming soon
Art. 95(6) Other Member States share additional information and any objections to notified national measures. Coming soon
Art. 95(7) Without objection within two months, national measures are deemed justified and replicated everywhere. Coming soon
Art. 96 Procedure for evaluating national measures at Union level
Art. 96(1) Commission evaluates national measures when objections arise and decides whether justified. Coming soon
Art. 96(2) Justified measures apply EU-wide; unjustified ones are withdrawn; silence after eight months means justified. Coming soon
Art. 96(3) Commission may adopt Union-level measures where national measures cannot satisfactorily mitigate a risk. Coming soon
Art. 97 Other non-compliance
Art. 97(1) Authorities require operators to end non-compliance that poses no unacceptable risk within a set period. Coming soon
Art. 97(2) If non-compliance persists, the Member State restricts, prohibits, recalls or withdraws the product and informs the Commission. Coming soon
Art. 97(3) The Commission may specify by implementing acts measures authorities take against given non-compliance types. Coming soon
Art. 98 Preventive health protection measures
Art. 98(1) A Member State may take justified measures against devices posing a potential risk after evaluation. Coming soon
Art. 98(2) A Member State must promptly notify the Commission and others of preventive measures with reasons. Coming soon
Art. 98(3) The Commission assesses national preventive measures and may decide whether they are justified; silence after six months means justified. Coming soon
Art. 98(4) The Commission may adopt Union-wide measures when assessment shows a device should be restricted or recalled everywhere. Coming soon
Art. 99 Good administrative practice
Art. 99(1) Authority measures must state grounds, be notified to the operator with remedies, or be published if general. Coming soon
Art. 99(2) Operators get a chance to make submissions before measures, except urgent risk cases, where review follows promptly. Coming soon
Art. 99(3) Measures are withdrawn or amended once the operator shows effective correction and compliance. Coming soon
Art. 99(4) Authorities inform the notified body and its authority of measures via the electronic system. Coming soon
Art. 100 Electronic system on market surveillance
Art. 100(1) The Commission and Member States set up an electronic market surveillance information system.
Art. 100(1)(a) The system holds summaries of surveillance activity results. Coming soon
Art. 100(1)(b) The system holds the final inspection report. Coming soon
Art. 100(1)(c) The system holds information on devices posing unacceptable health and safety risk. Coming soon
Art. 100(1)(d) The system holds information on product non-compliance. Coming soon
Art. 100(1)(e) The system holds information on preventive health protection measures. Coming soon
Art. 100(1)(f) The system holds summaries of reviews of Member States' surveillance activities. Coming soon
Art. 100(2) System information is immediately passed to relevant authorities and notified bodies and accessible to Member States and Commission. Coming soon
Art. 100(3) Information exchanged between Member States is withheld from the public if disclosure would harm surveillance. Coming soon
Art. 101 Competent authoritiesMember States designate and equip competent authorities and report them to the Commission for publication. Coming soon
Art. 102 Cooperation
Art. 102(1) Authorities cooperate with each other and the Commission, which organises information exchange. Coming soon
Art. 102(2) Member States take part in international regulatory cooperation initiatives where appropriate. Coming soon
Art. 103 Medical Device Coordination Group
Art. 103(1) A Medical Device Coordination Group is established. Coming soon
Art. 103(2) Each Member State appoints members and alternates with device expertise to the MDCG. Coming soon
Art. 103(3) The MDCG meets regularly and on request, attended by suitably expert members. Coming soon
Art. 103(4) The MDCG seeks consensus, otherwise majority vote, and records diverging positions on request. Coming soon
Art. 103(5) A Commission representative chairs the MDCG without voting. Coming soon
Art. 103(6) The MDCG may invite experts and third parties case by case. Coming soon
Art. 103(7) The MDCG may create sub-groups, with industry and stakeholder observers invited where suitable. Coming soon
Art. 103(8) The MDCG sets rules of procedure covering opinions, delegation, conflicts of interest and sub-groups. Coming soon
Art. 103(9) MDCG tasks are those set in this Regulation's Article 105 and the IVDR's Article 99. Coming soon
Art. 104 Support by the CommissionThe Commission supports authority cooperation and provides MDCG logistic, technical and scientific support. Coming soon
Art. 105 Tasks of the MDCGIntroduces the list of MDCG tasks.
Art. 105(a) MDCG helps assess applicant conformity assessment bodies and notified bodies. Coming soon
Art. 105(b) MDCG advises the Commission on the notified bodies coordination group when asked. Coming soon
Art. 105(c) MDCG helps develop guidance for harmonised implementation of the Regulation. Coming soon
Art. 105(d) MDCG helps monitor technical progress and whether safety and performance requirements remain adequate. Coming soon
Art. 105(e) MDCG helps develop standards, common specifications and clinical investigation guidelines. Coming soon
Art. 105(f) MDCG assists authorities in coordination, including a European market surveillance programme. Coming soon
Art. 105(g) MDCG gives advice on implementation issues on its own initiative or on request. Coming soon
Art. 105(h) MDCG contributes to harmonised administrative practice across Member States. Coming soon
Art. 106 Provision of scientific, technical and clinical opinions and advice
Art. 106(1) The Commission provides for designating expert panels and laboratories under principles of competence and independence. Coming soon
Art. 106(2) Expert panels and laboratories may be designated where consistent advice is needed, standing or temporary. Coming soon
Art. 106(3) Expert panels comprise Commission-appointed advisors who act impartially and declare interests publicly. Coming soon
Art. 106(4) Panels consider information from stakeholders such as patient organisations and professionals. Coming soon
Art. 106(5) The Commission may appoint panel advisors after a public call, for renewable three-year terms. Coming soon
Art. 106(6) The Commission may keep a published central list of available experts. Coming soon
Art. 106(7) The Commission may designate expert laboratories on application by a Member State or JRC. Coming soon
Art. 106(8) Expert laboratories must meet listed criteria.
Art. 106(8)(a) Expert laboratories need adequately qualified and experienced staff. Coming soon
Art. 106(8)(b) Expert laboratories need the equipment for their assigned tasks. Coming soon
Art. 106(8)(c) Expert laboratories need knowledge of international standards and best practice. Coming soon
Art. 106(8)(d) Expert laboratories need suitable administrative organisation and structure. Coming soon
Art. 106(8)(e) Expert laboratories must ensure staff keep information confidential. Coming soon
Art. 106(9) Clinical evaluation expert panels perform the tasks set in named articles and annexes. Coming soon
Art. 106(10) Introduces possible tasks of expert panels and laboratories.
Art. 106(10)(a) Provide scientific, technical and clinical assistance to the Commission and MDCG. Coming soon
Art. 106(10)(b) Contribute to guidance and common specifications for investigations, evaluation and testing. Coming soon
Art. 106(10)(c) Develop and review clinical and performance evaluation guidance reflecting the state of the art. Coming soon
Art. 106(10)(d) Contribute to international standards reflecting the state of the art. Coming soon
Art. 106(10)(e) Give opinions in response to consultations from manufacturers, notified bodies and Member States. Coming soon
Art. 106(10)(f) Contribute to identifying emerging safety and performance concerns. Coming soon
Art. 106(10)(g) Provide views on performance evaluation of certain in vitro diagnostic devices. Coming soon
Art. 106(11) The Commission facilitates access to expert advice on appropriate data sets for conformity assessment. Coming soon
Art. 106(12) Panels seek consensus or majority; the Commission publishes opinions with confidentiality considered. Coming soon
Art. 106(13) The Commission may charge manufacturers and notified bodies fees for expert advice, set by implementing act. Coming soon
Art. 106(14) Expert advice fees are transparent, cost-based, reduced for small enterprises, and paid to EMA or Commission. Coming soon
Art. 106(15) The Commission may amend expert panel and laboratory tasks by delegated acts. Coming soon
Art. 107 Conflict of interests
Art. 107(1) MDCG and expert members must have no impairing industry interests and publicly declare interests. Coming soon
Art. 107(2) Invited experts and third parties declare interests in the issue concerned. Coming soon
Art. 108 Device registers and databanksCommission and Member States encourage registers and databanks for specific device types. Coming soon
Art. 109 Confidentiality
Art. 109(1) All parties must keep information confidential to protect personal data, trade secrets and enforcement.
Art. 109(1)(a) Confidentiality protects personal data in line with Article 110. Coming soon
Art. 109(1)(b) Confidentiality protects commercial secrets and intellectual property unless disclosure serves public interest. Coming soon
Art. 109(1)(c) Confidentiality protects effective implementation, especially inspections, investigations and audits. Coming soon
Art. 109(2) Confidential information exchanged between authorities needs the originating authority's agreement before disclosure. Coming soon
Art. 109(3) Confidentiality does not limit information exchange, warnings or duties under criminal law. Coming soon
Art. 109(4) Confidential information may be shared with third-country regulators under confidentiality arrangements. Coming soon
Art. 110 Data protection
Art. 110(1) Member States apply the data protection directive to personal data processed under this Regulation. Coming soon
Art. 110(2) The EU institutions data protection regulation applies to Commission processing of personal data. Coming soon
Art. 111 Levying of fees
Art. 111(1) Member States may charge transparent, cost-recovery fees for activities under the Regulation. Coming soon
Art. 111(2) Member States give three months' notice of fee structure and make it available on request. Coming soon
Art. 112 Funding of activities related to designation and monitoring of notified bodiesThe Commission covers joint assessment costs and sets recoverable cost rules. Coming soon
Art. 113 PenaltiesMember States set effective, proportionate, dissuasive penalties and notify the Commission. Coming soon
Art. 114 Committee procedure
Art. 114(1) A Committee on Medical Devices assists the Commission. Coming soon
Art. 114(2) Where referenced, the advisory procedure of the comitology regulation applies. Coming soon
Art. 114(3) Where referenced, the examination procedure applies; no committee opinion means no act. Coming soon
Art. 114(4) Where referenced, the immediately applicable acts procedure applies with the other procedures. Coming soon
Art. 115 Exercise of the delegation
Art. 115(1) Commission's delegated act power is subject to this Article's conditions. Coming soon
Art. 115(2) Delegation lasts five years from 2017 and extends tacitly unless opposed. Coming soon
Art. 115(3) Parliament or Council may revoke the delegation at any time without affecting acts in force. Coming soon
Art. 115(4) The Commission consults Member State experts before adopting a delegated act. Coming soon
Art. 115(5) The Commission notifies adopted delegated acts simultaneously to Parliament and Council. Coming soon
Art. 115(6) Delegated acts take effect only if Parliament and Council raise no objection within three months. Coming soon
Art. 116 Separate delegated acts for different delegated powersThe Commission adopts a separate delegated act for each delegated power. Coming soon
Art. 117 Amendment to Directive 2001/83/ECAmends medicinal products directive annex on device conformity evidence in marketing authorisation dossiers.
Art. 117(12) Medicinal product dossiers must include device conformity results or a notified body opinion on the device part. Coming soon
Art. 118 Amendment to Regulation (EC) No 178/2002Amends the general food law regulation to exclude medical devices from its scope.
Art. 118(i) Adds medical devices to the list of items covered by the food law amendment. Coming soon
Art. 119 Amendment to Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009Amends the cosmetics regulation scope by adding a paragraph.
Art. 119(4) Commission may decide whether a product counts as a cosmetic, via the regulatory procedure. Coming soon
Art. 120 Transitional provisions
Art. 120(1) From May 2021, notified body notifications under the old directives become void. Coming soon
Art. 120(2) Certificates under old directives stay valid for limited periods, with conditions for expired ones.
Art. 120(2)(a) Condition: manufacturer and notified body signed a written conformity assessment agreement before certificate expiry. Coming soon
Art. 120(2)(b) Condition: authority granted a derogation or required the conformity assessment procedure. Coming soon
Art. 120(3) Legacy devices may be marketed until set dates if paragraph 3c conditions are met. Coming soon
Art. 120(3a) Legacy-certificate devices may stay on the market until dates by device class.
Art. 120(3a)(a) Class III and certain implantable IIb devices may be marketed until end of 2027. Coming soon
Art. 120(3a)(b) Other IIb, IIa and certain class I devices may be marketed until end of 2028. Coming soon
Art. 120(3b) Formerly self-declared devices now needing a notified body may be marketed until end of 2028. Coming soon
Art. 120(3c) Legacy devices may stay marketed only if listed conditions are met.
Art. 120(3c)(a) Legacy devices must keep complying with the old directives. Coming soon
Art. 120(3c)(b) No significant change to design or intended purpose. Coming soon
Art. 120(3c)(c) Devices must not present unacceptable risk to health or safety. Coming soon
Art. 120(3c)(d) Manufacturer must have a quality management system in place by May 2024. Coming soon
Art. 120(3c)(e) Formal notified body application by May 2024 and signed agreement by September 2024. Coming soon
Art. 120(3d) New post-market surveillance, vigilance and registration rules apply to legacy devices instead of old ones. Coming soon
Art. 120(3e) Issuing notified body keeps surveillance of certified devices unless transferred by agreement to another designated body. Coming soon
Art. 120(3f) Class III custom-made implants may be marketed until a set date without certificate if application and agreement deadlines met. Coming soon
Art. 120(4) Devices lawfully placed under earlier directives or transitional paragraphs may stay available on the market. Coming soon
Art. 120(5) Regulation-compliant devices may be placed on the market before the application date despite older directives. Coming soon
Art. 120(6) Conformity bodies may be designated and issue certificates under this Regulation before the application date. Coming soon
Art. 120(7) Transitional early application for consultation-procedure devices depends on MDCG and expert panel appointments being made. Coming soon
Art. 120(9) Authorisations granted under the old directives keep the validity stated in them. Coming soon
Art. 120(10) Certain legally marketed products newly brought into scope may continue to be marketed in the relevant Member States. Coming soon
Art. 120(11) Ongoing clinical investigations may continue, but serious event reporting follows this Regulation from the application date. Coming soon
Art. 120(12) Named issuing entities are treated as designated until the Commission designates entities. Coming soon
Art. 120(13) Article 10a also applies to devices covered by transitional paragraphs 3a and 3b. Coming soon
Art. 121 EvaluationCommission must evaluate the Regulation's application by a set date, focusing on UDI traceability. Coming soon
Art. 122 RepealEarlier directives are repealed from the application date, with exceptions for transitional devices and vigilance duties. Coming soon
Art. 123 Entry into force and date of application
Art. 123(1) Regulation enters into force twenty days after publication in the Official Journal. Coming soon
Art. 123(2) Regulation applies from 26 May 2021. Coming soon
Art. 123(3) Derogations from the general application date; Regulation is binding and directly applicable in all Member States.
Art. 123(3)(a) Notified body rules apply early to bodies that applied for designation. Coming soon
Art. 123(3)(b) Articles 101 and 103 apply from November 2017. Coming soon
Art. 123(3)(c) Article 102 applies from May 2018. Coming soon
Art. 123(3)(d) Eudamed-related obligations apply six months after notice that the system is functional. Coming soon
Art. 123(3)(e) Manufacturers must enter Article 29 information in Eudamed within twelve months of the functionality notice.
Art. 123(3)(e)(i) Eudamed entry duty covers non-custom devices assessed under Article 52. Coming soon
Art. 123(3)(e)(ii) Eudamed entry duty covers non-custom devices marketed under transitional provisions, unless already registered. Coming soon
Art. 123(3)(ea) Notified bodies must enter certificate information in Eudamed within eighteen months of the notice. Coming soon
Art. 123(3)(eb) Safety summary upload and authority notification duties apply to these devices once certificates are entered in Eudamed. Coming soon
Art. 123(3)(ec) Manufacturers submitting PSURs or vigilance reports must also register the device in Eudamed, except legacy devices. Coming soon
Art. 123(3)(f) UDI carrier duty under Article 27(4) phases in by device class from 2021 to 2025. Coming soon
Art. 123(3)(g) Phased dates for UDI carriers directly on reusable devices.
Art. 123(3)(g)(i) Direct UDI marking for reusable implantable and class III devices applies from May 2023. Coming soon
Art. 123(3)(g)(ii) Direct UDI marking for reusable class IIa and IIb devices applies from May 2025. Coming soon
Art. 123(3)(g)(iii) Direct UDI marking for reusable class I devices applies from May 2027. Coming soon
Art. 123(3)(i) Article 120(12) on issuing entities applies from May 2019. Coming soon
Art. 123(3)(j) Article 59 applies from April 2020. Coming soon
Annex I GENERAL SAFETY AND PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS
Annex I Chapter I GENERAL REQUIREMENTS
Annex I 1 Devices must perform as intended, be safe and effective, with risks acceptable against benefits. Coming soon
Annex I 2 Reducing risk as far as possible means without worsening the benefit-risk ratio. Coming soon
Annex I 3 Manufacturers must run a documented, continuous, iterative risk management system across the device lifecycle.
Annex I 3(a) Establish and document a risk management plan for each device. Coming soon
Annex I 3(b) Identify and analyse known and foreseeable hazards for each device. Coming soon
Annex I 3(c) Estimate and evaluate risks in intended use and foreseeable misuse. Coming soon
Annex I 3(d) Eliminate or control identified risks following Section 4 requirements. Coming soon
Annex I 3(e) Assess how production and post-market data affect hazards, risk estimates and acceptability. Coming soon
Annex I 3(f) Amend control measures where post-market evaluation shows it is necessary. Coming soon
Annex I 4 Risk controls must follow safety principles, leave acceptable residual risk, and residual risks be communicated to users.
Annex I 4(a) First priority: remove or reduce risks through safe design and manufacture. Coming soon
Annex I 4(b) Second priority: protective measures such as alarms for risks that cannot be removed. Coming soon
Annex I 4(c) Third priority: provide safety information and training to users. Coming soon
Annex I 5 Reduce use-error risks by considering ergonomics and intended users.
Annex I 5(a) Minimise risks from ergonomic features and the intended use environment. Coming soon
Annex I 5(b) Account for users' knowledge, training, conditions and setting, whether lay, professional or disabled. Coming soon
Annex I 6 Device performance must not degrade dangerously over its stated lifetime under normal stresses and maintenance. Coming soon
Annex I 7 Design and packaging must preserve performance through transport and storage conditions. Coming soon
Annex I 8 Known risks and side-effects must be minimised and acceptable versus benefits. Coming soon
Annex I 9 For Annex XVI products, safety means no risk or only the maximum acceptable risk. Coming soon
Annex I Chapter II REQUIREMENTS REGARDING DESIGN AND MANUFACTURE
Annex I 10 Chemical, physical and biological propertiesHeading for chemical, physical and biological property requirements.
Annex I 10.1 Design must ensure performance, paying attention to materials, compatibility, mechanical and surface properties.
Annex I 10.1(a) Choose materials considering toxicity and flammability. Coming soon
Annex I 10.1(b) Ensure materials are compatible with tissues, cells and body fluids. Coming soon
Annex I 10.1(c) Ensure compatibility between parts of multi-part implantable devices. Coming soon
Annex I 10.1(d) Consider how processing affects material properties. Coming soon
Annex I 10.1(e) Use validated biophysical or modelling research results where appropriate. Coming soon
Annex I 10.1(f) Consider mechanical properties such as strength, fatigue and wear resistance. Coming soon
Annex I 10.1(g) Consider surface properties of the device. Coming soon
Annex I 10.1(h) Confirm the device meets defined chemical or physical specifications. Coming soon
Annex I 10.2 Minimise contaminant and residue risk to patients and handlers. Coming soon
Annex I 10.3 Devices must be safe with materials they contact and compatible with medicinal products they administer. Coming soon
Annex I 10.4 Limit release of harmful substances; restrict CMR and endocrine-disrupting substances above threshold unless justified.
Annex I 10.4.1 Design and manufacture of devicesHeading identifying the substance categories covered by the restriction.
Annex I 10.4.1(a) Covers category 1A or 1B carcinogenic, mutagenic or reprotoxic substances. Coming soon
Annex I 10.4.1(b) Covers identified endocrine-disrupting substances affecting human health. Coming soon
Annex I 10.4.2 Justification regarding the presence of CMR and/or endocrine-disrupting substancesHeading for justification of CMR or endocrine-disrupting substances.
Annex I 10.4.2(a) Justification must analyse expected patient or user exposure to the substance. Coming soon
Annex I 10.4.2(b) Justification must analyse alternative substances, materials or designs and their availability. Coming soon
Annex I 10.4.2(c) Justify why substitutes or design changes are unsuitable, noting vulnerable patient groups. Coming soon
Annex I 10.4.2(d) Justification must consider latest relevant guidelines where available. Coming soon
Annex I 10.4.3 Guidelines on phthalatesHeading for guidelines on phthalates. Coming soon
Annex I 10.4.4 Guidelines on other CMR and endocrine-disrupting substancesHeading for guidelines on other CMR and endocrine-disrupting substances. Coming soon
Annex I 10.4.5 LabellingHeading for labelling of such substances. Coming soon
Annex I 10.5 Reduce risks from unintended ingress of substances into the device. Coming soon
Annex I 10.6 Reduce risks from released particles, with special attention to nanomaterials. Coming soon
Annex I 11 Infection and microbial contaminationHeading for infection and microbial contamination requirements.
Annex I 11.1 Design and manufacturing must eliminate or reduce infection risk to patients and users.
Annex I 11.1(a) Reduce risks of unintended cuts and pricks such as needle sticks. Coming soon
Annex I 11.1(b) Design must allow easy and safe handling. Coming soon
Annex I 11.1(c) Reduce microbial leakage and exposure during use. Coming soon
Annex I 11.1(d) Prevent microbial contamination of the device or its contents. Coming soon
Annex I 11.2 Design devices to allow safe cleaning, disinfection or re-sterilisation where needed. Coming soon
Annex I 11.3 Devices with a stated microbial state must keep it through transport and storage. Coming soon
Annex I 11.4 Sterile-delivered devices must stay sterile until packaging is opened, with evident packaging integrity. Coming soon
Annex I 11.5 Sterile-labelled devices must use appropriate validated processing and sterilisation methods. Coming soon
Annex I 11.6 Devices to be sterilised must be made in controlled conditions and facilities. Coming soon
Annex I 11.7 Non-sterile packaging must preserve cleanliness and suit the stated sterilisation method. Coming soon
Annex I 11.8 Labelling must distinguish sterile and non-sterile versions of similar devices. Coming soon
Annex I 12 Heading for devices with medicinal substances or absorbed substance-based devices.
Annex I 12.1 Verify quality, safety and usefulness of incorporated medicinal substance by analogy with the medicines directive. Coming soon
Annex I 12.2 Substance-based absorbed devices must meet relevant medicines directive requirements for aspects not covered here. Coming soon
Annex I 13 Devices incorporating materials of biological originHeading for devices incorporating materials of biological origin.
Annex I 13.1 Rules for devices using non-viable human tissue or cell derivatives.
Annex I 13.1(a) Donation, procurement and testing of human tissues must follow the tissue directive. Coming soon
Annex I 13.1(b) Process human-derived materials safely, with validated virus elimination or inactivation. Coming soon
Annex I 13.1(c) Traceability must be compatible with tissue and blood directives' traceability and data protection rules. Coming soon
Annex I 13.2 Rules for devices using non-viable animal tissues or cells.
Annex I 13.2(a) Animal tissues should come from veterinary-controlled animals; keep geographic origin information. Coming soon
Annex I 13.2(b) Handle animal-derived materials safely, with validated virus elimination or inactivation. Coming soon
Annex I 13.2(c) Animal-tissue devices must meet the specific requirements of Regulation 722/2012. Coming soon
Annex I 13.3 Other non-viable biological substances must be handled safely, including virus elimination and waste disposal. Coming soon
Annex I 14 Construction of devices and interaction with their environmentHeading for construction of devices and interaction with environment.
Annex I 14.1 Combinations of devices must be safe, with restrictions labelled and connections designed against misconnection. Coming soon
Annex I 14.2 Design must remove or reduce a list of physical and environmental risks.
Annex I 14.2(a) Reduce injury risk from physical and ergonomic features. Coming soon
Annex I 14.2(b) Reduce risks from foreseeable external influences such as electromagnetic effects, pressure and temperature. Coming soon
Annex I 14.2(c) Reduce risks from contact with materials, liquids and gases during use. Coming soon
Annex I 14.2(d) Reduce risks from negative interaction between software and its IT environment. Coming soon
Annex I 14.2(e) Reduce risks from accidental ingress of substances. Coming soon
Annex I 14.2(f) Reduce risks of mutual interference with other devices used alongside. Coming soon
Annex I 14.2(g) Reduce risks from ageing or lost accuracy where maintenance or calibration is impossible. Coming soon
Annex I 14.3 Minimise fire or explosion risk in normal use and single fault. Coming soon
Annex I 14.4 Design so adjustment, calibration and maintenance can be done safely and effectively. Coming soon
Annex I 14.5 Devices working with other products must have reliable and safe interoperability and compatibility. Coming soon
Annex I 14.6 Measurement, monitoring and display scales must follow ergonomic principles. Coming soon
Annex I 14.7 Design for safe disposal; identify, test and describe disposal procedures in instructions. Coming soon
Annex I 15 Devices with a diagnostic or measuring functionHeading for requirements on diagnostic and measuring devices.
Annex I 15.1 Diagnostic and measuring devices must be accurate, precise and stable, with accuracy limits stated. Coming soon
Annex I 15.2 Measurements must be shown in legally recognised units of measurement. Coming soon
Annex I 16 Protection against radiationHeading for requirements on protection against radiation.
Annex I 16.1 GeneralSubheading for general radiation protection requirements.
Annex I 16.1(a) Design and package devices so radiation exposure is minimised while still allowing needed therapeutic levels. Coming soon
Annex I 16.1(b) Instructions for radiation-emitting devices must describe the radiation, protections, misuse avoidance, testing and maintenance. Coming soon
Annex I 16.2 Intended radiationSubheading for deliberately emitted radiation.
Annex I 16.2(a) Devices emitting hazardous radiation deliberately must let users control emissions with reproducible parameters. Coming soon
Annex I 16.2(b) Devices emitting hazardous radiation should have visual or audible emission warnings where possible. Coming soon
Annex I 16.3 Reduce exposure to stray, scattered or unintended radiation as far as possible. Coming soon
Annex I 16.4 Ionising radiationSubheading for ionising radiation requirements.
Annex I 16.4(a) Ionising radiation devices must reflect the EU basic safety standards directive. Coming soon
Annex I 16.4(b) Ionising emitters should allow radiation quantity, geometry and quality to be varied, controlled and monitored. Coming soon
Annex I 16.4(c) Diagnostic radiology devices must give adequate image quality with minimal exposure. Coming soon
Annex I 16.4(d) Therapeutic radiology devices must allow reliable monitoring and control of dose, beam type and energy. Coming soon
Annex I 17 Electronic programmable systems — devices that incorporate electronic programmable systems and software that are devices in themselvesHeading for programmable electronic systems and software that are devices themselves.
Annex I 17.1 Programmable systems and software must be repeatable, reliable, performant, and mitigate risk from single faults. Coming soon
Annex I 17.2 Software must follow state-of-the-art lifecycle, risk management including information security, verification and validation. We detect

secrets.committedCommitting credentials is not software development to the state of the art in information security.

secrets.in-historyA leaked, unrotated credential shows information-security risk is not managed in development.

secrets.insecure-defaultShipping a usable sample value for the software's own signing secret is not development to the state of the art in information security.

tls.verification-disabledDisabling certificate checks falls below the state of the art in information security for device software.
Annex I 17.3 Mobile-platform software must account for screen characteristics and varying use environments. Coming soon
Annex I 17.4 Manufacturers must specify minimum hardware, network and IT security requirements for running the software. Coming soon
Annex I 18 Active devices and devices connected to themHeading for active devices and devices connected to them.
Annex I 18.1 Non-implantable active devices must reduce risks from a single fault condition. Coming soon
Annex I 18.2 Devices depending on internal power must indicate power state and warn when capacity is critical. Coming soon
Annex I 18.3 Devices depending on external power must have an alarm for power failure. Coming soon
Annex I 18.4 Patient-monitoring devices must have alarms for situations risking death or severe deterioration. Coming soon
Annex I 18.5 Reduce risk of electromagnetic interference that could impair this or other equipment. Coming soon
Annex I 18.6 Devices need adequate intrinsic immunity to electromagnetic interference to operate as intended. Coming soon
Annex I 18.7 Avoid accidental electric shock in normal use and single fault conditions. Coming soon
Annex I 18.8 Protect devices against unauthorised access that could stop them working as intended. We detect

tls.verification-disabledTurning off certificate checks lets network attackers impersonate endpoints and alter traffic, a direct design failure against intrusion affecting device operation.
Annex I 19 Particular requirements for active implantable devicesHeading for particular requirements for active implantable devices.
Annex I 19.1 Active implantable devices must minimise listed energy, treatment and maintenance-related risks.
Annex I 19.1(a) Minimise risks from energy sources, such as insulation, leakage currents and overheating. Coming soon
Annex I 19.1(b) Minimise risks from treatments like defibrillators or high-frequency surgical equipment. Coming soon
Annex I 19.1(c) Minimise risks where maintenance and calibration are impossible, such as ageing and reduced accuracy. Coming soon
Annex I 19.2 Ensure compatibility with administered substances and a reliable energy source. Coming soon
Annex I 19.3 Implantable devices and components must be identifiable to allow follow-up action on risks. Coming soon
Annex I 19.4 Implants must carry a code identifying device and manufacturer, readable without surgery. Coming soon
Annex I 20 Protection against mechanical and thermal risksHeading for protection against mechanical and thermal risks.
Annex I 20.1 Protect patients and users from mechanical risks like instability and moving parts. Coming soon
Annex I 20.2 Reduce vibration risks to the lowest level, unless part of specified performance. Coming soon
Annex I 20.3 Reduce risks from emitted noise to the lowest level, unless part of performance. Coming soon

Annex I 20.5 Make fitting errors of risky parts impossible by design or mark them clearly. Coming soon
Annex I 20.6 Accessible device parts must not reach dangerous temperatures in normal use. Coming soon
Annex I 21 Protection against the risks posed to the patient or user by devices supplying energy or substancesHeading for risks from devices supplying energy or substances.
Annex I 21.1 Delivered amount of energy or substance must be settable and maintainable accurately enough for safety. Coming soon
Annex I 21.2 Devices must prevent or indicate inadequate delivery and accidental release of dangerous energy or substances. Coming soon
Annex I 21.3 Controls and indicators must be clearly specified and operating information understandable to users. Coming soon
Annex I 22 Protection against the risks posed by medical devices intended by the manufacturer for use by lay personsHeading for protection against risks of devices intended for lay persons.
Annex I 22.1 Lay-person devices must perform despite users' limited skills and variable technique; instructions easy to follow. Coming soon
Annex I 22.2 Lay-person devices must support safe accurate use, limit injuries and reduce handling or interpretation errors. Coming soon
Annex I 22.3 Lay-person devices should let users verify performance and warn of invalid results. Coming soon
Annex I Chapter III REQUIREMENTS REGARDING THE INFORMATION SUPPLIED WITH THE DEVICE
Annex I 23 Label and instructions for useHeading for label and instructions for use.
Annex I 23.1 General requirements regarding the information supplied by the manufacturerDevices need identifying and safety information, kept current on the manufacturer's website.
Annex I 23.1(a) Label and instruction format and content must suit the device and intended users' knowledge. Coming soon
Annex I 23.1(b) Label information goes on the device, or on packaging if impracticable. Coming soon
Annex I 23.1(c) Labels must be human-readable, optionally supplemented by machine-readable codes. Coming soon
Annex I 23.1(d) Instructions accompany devices, except low-risk classes that can be used safely without them. Coming soon
Annex I 23.1(e) One instruction copy may serve multiple devices supplied to one user if agreed. Coming soon
Annex I 23.1(f) Electronic instructions are allowed only under the conditions of the referenced regulation. Coming soon
Annex I 23.1(g) Residual risks to be communicated appear as limitations, contra-indications, precautions or warnings. Coming soon
Annex I 23.1(h) Use internationally recognised symbols conforming to harmonised standards, or describe them in documentation. Coming soon
Annex I 23.2 Information on the labelIntroduces the particulars the label must bear.
Annex I 23.2(a) Label shows the device name or trade name. Coming soon
Annex I 23.2(b) Label gives details to identify device, pack contents and intended purpose if unclear. Coming soon
Annex I 23.2(c) Label shows manufacturer's name and registered business address. Coming soon
Annex I 23.2(d) Non-EU manufacturers' labels name the authorised representative and its address. Coming soon
Annex I 23.2(e) Label states if device contains medicinal substances or human or animal tissues. Coming soon
Annex I 23.2(f) Label carries information required by the referenced section on certain substances. Coming soon
Annex I 23.2(g) Label shows lot or serial number with identifying words or symbol. Coming soon
Annex I 23.2(h) Label bears the unique device identification carrier. Coming soon
Annex I 23.2(i) Label gives an unambiguous safe-use or implant-by date, where relevant. Coming soon
Annex I 23.2(j) Without an expiry date, label shows manufacture date, possibly within lot number. Coming soon
Annex I 23.2(k) Label indicates any special storage or handling conditions. Coming soon
Annex I 23.2(l) Sterile devices' labels state sterile status and sterilisation method. Coming soon
Annex I 23.2(m) Label carries warnings needing immediate attention, with detail in instructions. Coming soon
Annex I 23.2(n) Single-use devices must be labelled as such, consistently across the Union. Coming soon
Annex I 23.2(o) Reprocessed single-use devices state that fact, cycles done and cycle limits. Coming soon
Annex I 23.2(p) Custom-made devices carry the words 'custom-made device'. Coming soon
Annex I 23.2(q) Label states it is a medical device, or clinical-investigation-only wording. Coming soon
Annex I 23.2(r) Substance-based devices' labels give composition and quantity of main active constituents. Coming soon
Annex I 23.2(s) Implantable devices' labels show serial number, or lot number for non-active implants. Coming soon
Annex I 23.3 Information on the packaging which maintains the sterile condition of a device (‘sterile packaging’)Introduces particulars required on sterile packaging.
Annex I 23.3(a) Sterile packaging must be recognisable as such. Coming soon
Annex I 23.3(b) Packaging declares the device is sterile. Coming soon
Annex I 23.3(c) Packaging states the sterilisation method. Coming soon
Annex I 23.3(d) Packaging shows manufacturer's name and address. Coming soon
Annex I 23.3(e) Packaging includes a description of the device. Coming soon
Annex I 23.3(f) Clinical-investigation devices' packaging carries the investigation-only wording. Coming soon
Annex I 23.3(g) Custom-made devices' packaging carries the custom-made wording. Coming soon
Annex I 23.3(h) Packaging shows month and year of manufacture. Coming soon
Annex I 23.3(i) Packaging gives an unambiguous safe-use time limit in year and month. Coming soon
Annex I 23.3(j) Packaging tells users to check instructions if packaging is damaged or opened. Coming soon
Annex I 23.4 Information in the instructions for useIntroduces particulars the instructions for use must contain.
Annex I 23.4(a) Instructions repeat several specified label particulars. Coming soon
Annex I 23.4(b) Instructions specify intended purpose, indications, contra-indications, patient groups and intended users. Coming soon
Annex I 23.4(c) Instructions specify expected clinical benefits where applicable. Coming soon
Annex I 23.4(d) Instructions link to the safety and clinical performance summary where applicable. Coming soon
Annex I 23.4(e) Instructions state the device's performance characteristics. Coming soon
Annex I 23.4(f) Instructions help professionals verify suitability and choose matching software and accessories. Coming soon
Annex I 23.4(g) Instructions list residual risks, contra-indications and side-effects, including patient information. Coming soon
Annex I 23.4(h) Instructions give specifications for proper use, such as claimed measuring accuracy. Coming soon
Annex I 23.4(i) Instructions detail preparation before use, such as sterilisation, assembly, calibration and disinfection. Coming soon
Annex I 23.4(j) Instructions state needed special facilities, training or user qualifications. Coming soon
Annex I 23.4(k) Instructions give installation verification, maintenance, consumables, calibration and servicing risk information. Coming soon
Annex I 23.4(l) Sterile devices' instructions explain what to do if packaging is damaged. Coming soon
Annex I 23.4(m) Non-sterile devices to be sterilised need appropriate sterilisation instructions. Coming soon
Annex I 23.4(n) Reusable devices need reprocessing instructions and indicators of when to stop reuse. Coming soon
Annex I 23.4(o) Indicate if reuse requires reconditioning under the manufacturer's responsibility. Coming soon
Annex I 23.4(p) Single-use devices' instructions describe risks of reuse, based on risk management documentation. Coming soon
Annex I 23.4(q) Instructions identify compatible devices or equipment and known combination restrictions. Coming soon
Annex I 23.4(r) Radiation-emitting devices' instructions describe the radiation and protection from unintended exposure. Coming soon
Annex I 23.4(s) Instructions convey warnings, precautions, contra-indications and limitations, including malfunction and environmental influences. Coming soon
Annex I 23.4(t) Substance-based devices' instructions cover interactions, side-effects, contra-indications and overdose risks. Coming soon
Annex I 23.4(u) Implantable devices' instructions give qualitative and quantitative material and substance exposure information. Coming soon
Annex I 23.4(v) Instructions give warnings for safe disposal, covering infection and sharps hazards. Coming soon
Annex I 23.4(w) Lay-person devices' instructions say when to consult a healthcare professional. Coming soon
Annex I 23.4(x) Devices without medical purpose must state absence of clinical benefit and related risks. Coming soon
Annex I 23.4(y) Instructions show issue date, or revision date and identifier of latest revision. Coming soon
Annex I 23.4(z) Instructions must tell users to report serious incidents to manufacturer and their national authority. Coming soon
Annex I 23.4(aa) Instructions must include information for patients with implanted devices, as set out in Article 18. Coming soon
Annex I 23.4(ab) Software instructions must state minimum hardware, network characteristics and IT security measures, including unauthorised-access protection. Coming soon
Annex II TECHNICAL DOCUMENTATIONTechnical documentation must be clear, organised, searchable and unambiguous, containing the listed elements.
Annex II 1 DEVICE DESCRIPTION AND SPECIFICATION, INCLUDING VARIANTS AND ACCESSORIESTechnical documentation section covering device description, specification, variants and accessories.
Annex II 1.1 Device description and specificationSubsection heading for device description and specification content.
Annex II 1.1(a) Document the product name, general description, intended purpose and intended users. Coming soon
Annex II 1.1(b) Record the Basic UDI-DI or another unambiguous traceable identifier for the device. Coming soon
Annex II 1.1(c) Document target patients, conditions, selection criteria, indications, contra-indications and warnings. Coming soon
Annex II 1.1(d) Describe how the device works and its mode of action, with scientific demonstration. Coming soon
Annex II 1.1(e) Explain why the product qualifies as a medical device. Coming soon
Annex II 1.1(f) State the risk class and justify the classification rules applied. Coming soon
Annex II 1.1(g) Explain any novel features of the device. Coming soon
Annex II 1.1(h) Describe accessories and other products intended for use in combination with the device. Coming soon
Annex II 1.1(i) List or describe all configurations and variants to be marketed. Coming soon
Annex II 1.1(j) Describe key functional elements, including software, with labelled diagrams and explanations. Coming soon
Annex II 1.1(k) Describe raw materials in key elements and those contacting the body. Coming soon
Annex II 1.1(l) Provide technical specifications such as features, dimensions and performance for variants and accessories. Coming soon
Annex II 1.2 Reference to previous and similar generations of the deviceSubsection heading for referencing previous and similar device generations.
Annex II 1.2(a) Give an overview of the manufacturer's earlier generations of the device. Coming soon
Annex II 1.2(b) Give an overview of similar devices on Union or international markets. Coming soon
Annex II 2 INFORMATION TO BE SUPPLIED BY THE MANUFACTURERDocumentation must include the complete information supplied by the manufacturer, such as labels and instructions. Coming soon
Annex II 3 DESIGN AND MANUFACTURING INFORMATIONSection on design and manufacturing information.
Annex II 3(a) Provide information allowing the design stages applied to be understood. Coming soon
Annex II 3(b) Include full manufacturing process specifications, validation, monitoring and final testing data. Coming soon
Annex II 3(c) Identify all design and manufacturing sites, including suppliers and subcontractors. Coming soon
Annex II 4 GENERAL SAFETY AND PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTSDocumentation must demonstrate conformity with applicable general safety and performance requirements, with justification, validation and verification.
Annex II 4(a) List applicable safety and performance requirements and explain why others do not apply. Coming soon
Annex II 4(b) State the methods used to show conformity with each applicable requirement. Coming soon
Annex II 4(c) Identify harmonised standards, common specifications or other solutions applied. Coming soon
Annex II 4(d) Identify controlled evidence documents per standard, cross-referenced to their location in the documentation. Coming soon
Annex II 5 BENEFIT-RISK ANALYSIS AND RISK MANAGEMENTDocumentation must contain benefit-risk analysis and risk management information.
Annex II 5(a) Include the benefit-risk analysis required by Annex I Sections 1 and 8. Coming soon
Annex II 5(b) Include risk management solutions adopted and their results. Coming soon
Annex II 6 PRODUCT VERIFICATION AND VALIDATIONDocumentation must contain results and critical analysis of all verification and validation testing.
Annex II 6.1 Pre-clinical and clinical dataSubsection heading for pre-clinical and clinical data.
Annex II 6.1(a) Provide pre-clinical test results and literature evaluation on safety and conformity with specifications. Coming soon
Annex II 6.1(b) Provide detailed test designs, protocols and conclusions, including software verification and validation across configurations. Coming soon
Annex II 6.1(c) Include the clinical evaluation report, its updates and the clinical evaluation plan. Coming soon
Annex II 6.1(d) Include the PMCF plan and report, or justify why PMCF does not apply. Coming soon
Annex II 6.2 Additional information required in specific casesSubsection heading for extra information required in specific cases.
Annex II 6.2(a) For devices with a medicinal substance, state this and give source and safety data. Coming soon
Annex II 6.2(b) For devices using human or animal tissues or cells, state this and show conformity. Coming soon
Annex II 6.2(c) For absorbed or dispersed substance-based devices, provide absorption, interaction, tolerance and toxicity studies or a justification. Coming soon
Annex II 6.2(d) For devices with CMR or endocrine-disrupting substances, include the required justification. Coming soon
Annex II 6.2(e) For sterile or defined-microbiological-condition devices, describe manufacturing environment and sterility methods with validation reports. Coming soon
Annex II 6.2(f) For devices with a measuring function, describe methods ensuring the specified accuracy. Coming soon
Annex II 6.2(g) For devices connected to others, describe the combination and prove conformity when connected. Coming soon
Annex III TECHNICAL DOCUMENTATION ON POST-MARKET SURVEILLANCEPost-market surveillance technical documentation must be clear, organised, searchable and include the listed elements.
Annex III 1 Include a post-market surveillance plan proving compliance with the surveillance obligation.
Annex III 1(a) Surveillance plan must cover collecting incident, complaint, literature and similar-device information. Coming soon
Annex III 1(b) Surveillance plan must define processes, indicators, complaint investigation, trend methods, communication, corrective actions and traceability. Coming soon
Annex III 2 Include the periodic safety update report and post-market surveillance report. Coming soon

Annex IV 7 Declaration references any common specifications used for conformity. Coming soon

Annex VI Part A 2.6 Registration indicates whether the device is a reprocessed single-use device. Coming soon

Annex VI Part A 2.10 Registration indicates presence of animal tissues or cells or derivatives. Coming soon

Annex VI Part C THE UDI SYSTEM
Annex VI Part C 1 DefinitionsDefines UDI terms such as AIDC, Basic UDI-DI, unit of use DI, configurable device. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 2 General requirementsHeading for general UDI requirements.
Annex VI Part C 2.1 UDI affixing is additional to, and does not replace, other labelling requirements. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 2.2 Manufacturer must assign and maintain unique UDIs for its devices. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 2.3 Only the manufacturer may put the UDI on device or packaging. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 2.4 Only coding standards from Commission-designated issuing entities may be used. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 3 The UDISection heading introducing the rules on the unique device identifier.
Annex VI Part C 3.1 Device or its packaging gets a UDI; each higher packaging level needs its own. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 3.2 Shipping containers and logistics units need no UDI. Coming soon

Annex VI Part C 3.5 Lot, serial, software identification or expiry shown on label belongs in production identifier. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 3.6 Separately sold device components need their own UDI, unless part of a UDI-marked configurable device. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 3.7 Systems and procedure packs must be assigned and carry their own UDI. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 3.8 Manufacturers assign UDIs according to the applicable coding standard. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 3.9 Changes risking misidentification or traceability ambiguity require a new device identifier.
Annex VI Part C 3.9(a) Changing the name or trade name requires a new device identifier. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 3.9(b) Changing the device version or model requires a new device identifier. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 3.9(c) Changing single-use labelling requires a new device identifier. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 3.9(d) Changing whether the device is packaged sterile requires a new device identifier. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 3.9(e) Changing whether sterilisation is needed before use requires a new device identifier. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 3.9(f) Changing the quantity of devices per package requires a new device identifier. Coming soon

Annex VI Part C 4.2 With severe space limits, the carrier may go on the next packaging level up. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 4.3 Individually packaged class I and IIa single-use devices may carry the carrier on outer packaging. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 4.4 Retail point-of-sale devices need not show machine-readable production identifiers on packaging. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 4.5 Where other machine-readable codes are on the label, the UDI must be easy to identify. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 4.6 Linear bar codes may split or join identifiers, but each element must be distinguishable. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 4.7 Under tight space limits only machine-readable form is required, except home-use devices need readable text. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 4.8 Human-readable format follows the issuing entity's rules. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 4.9 If RFID is used, a standard bar code must also appear on the label. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 4.10 Reusable devices carry a durable UDI on the device itself, with limited exceptions.

Annex VI Part C 4.10(b) Exception: direct marking is technologically infeasible. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 4.11 The carrier must stay readable in normal use throughout the device's lifetime. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 4.12 No packaging carrier needed if the carrier can be read or scanned through packaging. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 4.13 For multi-part devices assembled before first use, one part carrying the carrier suffices. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 4.14 Carrier must be positioned so machine reading works during normal operation or storage. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 4.15 Bar codes holding both identifiers may also hold operating or other data. Coming soon

Annex VI Part C 5.2 Manufacturers submit and update device identification data in the UDI database. Coming soon

Annex VII 1.2.3 Notified body, management and assessors must avoid listed conflicting roles and activities.

Annex VII 1.2.3(b) Must not take part in design, manufacture, marketing or use of devices designated. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.2.3(c) Must avoid activities that conflict with independent judgement or integrity. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.2.3(d) Must not provide services, especially consultancy, undermining confidence in impartiality. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.2.3(e) Must not be linked to consultancy organisations; generic training is permitted. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.2.4 Prior consultancy must be documented; ex-client staff barred from that client for three years. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.2.5 Pay must not depend on assessment results; management interest declarations are public. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.2.6 Publicly owned notified bodies must document independence from responsible authorities. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.2.7 Notified body documents that subsidiaries, subcontractors and owners do not compromise its impartiality. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.2.8 Fair, consistent terms, with fees considering small and medium-sized enterprises. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.2.9 Technical and regulatory exchanges with applying manufacturers remain permitted. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.3 ConfidentialityHeading for notified body confidentiality.
Annex VII 1.3.1 Documented procedures ensure staff and partners keep assessment information confidential. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.3.2 Staff observe professional secrecy, protecting proprietary rights, with documented procedures. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.4 LiabilityHeading for notified body liability.
Annex VII 1.4.1 Notified body must carry liability insurance unless the Member State assumes liability. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.4.2 Insurance scope and value must match activities and risk, including certificate withdrawals. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.5 Financial requirementsNotified body must have and evidence adequate finances and long-term viability. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.6 Participation in coordination activitiesHeading for participation in coordination activities.
Annex VII 1.6.1 Notified body takes part in standardisation and coordination work and keeps staff informed. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.6.2 Notified body must consider guidance and best-practice documents. Coming soon
Annex VII 2 QUALITY MANAGEMENT REQUIREMENTSHeading for notified body quality management requirements.
Annex VII 2.1 Notified body maintains a documented quality management system suited to its activities. Coming soon
Annex VII 2.2 Notified body's quality system must cover documentation, records, audits, reviews, corrective actions, complaints and training. Coming soon
Annex VII 2.3 Notified body top management must ensure its quality system is understood and maintained across subsidiaries and subcontractors. Coming soon
Annex VII 2.4 Notified body staff must sign commitments on confidentiality, independence and impartiality, with written compliance statements. Coming soon
Annex VII 3 RESOURCE REQUIREMENTSHeading introducing the resource requirements section for notified bodies.
Annex VII 3.1 GeneralHeading for general resource requirements of notified bodies.
Annex VII 3.1.1 Notified bodies need enough competent personnel, equipment and facilities to perform all designated conformity assessment tasks with integrity. Coming soon
Annex VII 3.1.2 Notified body must keep staff expertise current through experience exchange and ongoing training programmes. Coming soon
Annex VII 3.1.3 Notified body must document and communicate personnel duties, limits and authorisation levels, including subcontractors and external experts. Coming soon
Annex VII 3.2 Qualification criteria in relation to personnelHeading for personnel qualification criteria of notified bodies.
Annex VII 3.2.1 Notified body must document qualification criteria and procedures for selecting and authorising assessment personnel. Coming soon
Annex VII 3.2.2 Qualification criteria must follow the designation scope, with specific criteria for listed assessment areas such as software. Coming soon
Annex VII 3.2.3 Staff who set qualification criteria and authorise others must be in-house with proven legislative and technical knowledge. Coming soon
Annex VII 3.2.4 Notified body must have permanent clinical expertise integrated into assessment and able to challenge clinical evaluations. Coming soon
Annex VII 3.2.5 Product reviewers must hold relevant degrees, four years' experience and knowledge of legislation, standards, risk and clinical evaluation. Coming soon
Annex VII 3.2.6 Site auditors need relevant degrees, experience in quality management, auditing training and reporting ability. Coming soon
Annex VII 3.2.7 Final reviewers and certification decision-makers must be employed in-house with comprehensive collective knowledge and experience. Coming soon
Annex VII 3.3 Documentation of qualification, training and authorisation of personnelHeading for documenting personnel qualification, training and authorisation.
Annex VII 3.3.1 Notified body needs a procedure documenting each person's qualifications; exceptions must be justified to the authority. Coming soon
Annex VII 3.3.2 Keep current authorisation matrix and knowledge records for key personnel, with rationale and activity records. Coming soon
Annex VII 3.4 Subcontractors and external expertsHeading for subcontractors and external experts.
Annex VII 3.4.1 Notified bodies may subcontract only defined parts, never whole audits or final decisions, and stay responsible. Coming soon
Annex VII 3.4.2 Subcontracting requires a policy, no onward subcontracting, written agreements, documentation and full notified body responsibility. Coming soon
Annex VII 3.4.3 When using external experts, notified body keeps internal competence to lead assessment and verify expert opinions. Coming soon
Annex VII 3.5 Monitoring of competences, training and exchange of experienceHeading for monitoring competences, training and experience exchange.
Annex VII 3.5.1 Notified body needs procedures to evaluate and continuously monitor internal and external personnel and subcontractors. Coming soon
Annex VII 3.5.2 Regularly review staff competence, identify training needs and plan training, checking awareness of law and standards. Coming soon
Annex VII 4 PROCESS REQUIREMENTSHeading introducing process requirements for notified bodies.
Annex VII 4.1 GeneralNotified body needs documented, detailed procedures for each conformity assessment step; some steps cannot be subcontracted. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.2 Notified body quotations and pre-application activitiesIntroduces notified body duties on quotations and pre-application activities.
Annex VII 4.2(a) Publish a public description of the application procedure and acceptable languages. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.2(b) Document procedures and details on fees and financial conditions for assessments. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.2(c) Document advertising procedures so promotion never suggests faster, easier or laxer certification. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.2(d) Review pre-application information, including scope and classification, before issuing any quotation. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.2(e) Contracts must be concluded directly between manufacturer and notified body, with no other organisation. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.3 Application review and contractRequire signed application and written contract; document procedures and outcomes of application reviews.
Annex VII 4.3(a) Application review must check completeness against the relevant conformity assessment procedure. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.3(b) Application review must verify the product qualifies as a device and its classification. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.3(c) Application review must confirm the chosen procedure applies to the device. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.3(d) Application review must confirm the notified body's designation covers the assessment. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.3(e) Application review must confirm sufficient, appropriate resources are available. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.4 Allocation of resourcesNotified body must allocate qualified personnel per application, name a responsible individual, and document task allocation. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.5 Conformity assessment activitiesHeading for conformity assessment activities.
Annex VII 4.5.1 GeneralConduct assessments with integrity and competence, using documented procedures and considering available specifications and standards. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.5.2 Quality management system auditingHeading for quality management system auditing.
Annex VII 4.5.2(a) Before audits, plan the audit programme, sites, suppliers, audit plans, sampling plan and assign qualified staff. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.5.2(b) Audit manufacturer's quality system and key processes, sampling documentation according to risk, per documented procedures. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.5.3 Product verificationNotified body needs expertise, facilities and procedures for technical documentation assessment and type-examination.
Annex VII 4.5.3(a) Verification by examination and testing of every productHave procedures, expertise and facilities for per-product verification by examination and testing. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.5.3(b) Verification by examination and testing of every productEstablish test plan of critical parameters to verify conformity for class IIb and IIa devices. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.5.3(c) Verification by examination and testing of every productDocument the reasoning for choosing the test parameters. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.5.3(d) Verification by examination and testing of every productHave procedures for assessments and tests verifying conformity by examining every product. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.5.3(e) Verification by examination and testing of every productHave procedures for agreeing with the applicant on tests performed elsewhere. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.5.3(f) Verification by examination and testing of every productTake full responsibility for test results; accept manufacturer reports only from competent independent bodies. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.5.4 Pre-clinical evaluation assessmentNotified body must have procedures to review and critically examine manufacturer's pre-clinical evaluation.
Annex VII 4.5.4(a) Manufacturer's pre-clinical evaluation planning, literature search and testing must be adequately addressed. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.5.4(b) Assess nature and duration of body contact and related biological risks. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.5.4(c) Assess the pre-clinical evaluation's interface with risk management. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.5.4(d) Appraise available pre-clinical data and its relevance to Annex I conformity. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.5.5 Clinical evaluation assessmentNotified body must have procedures to assess manufacturers' clinical evaluation, initially and ongoing, per Annex XIV. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.5.6 Specific ProceduresNotified body needs procedures for specific assessments, including animal-origin tissue devices under the TSE regulation. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.6 ReportingNotified body reporting duties on assessment reports. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.7 Final reviewNotified body must perform a final review before making its decision. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.8 Decisions and CertificationsNotified body needs documented decision procedures for issuing, suspending, restricting and withdrawing certificates. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.9 Changes and modificationsNotified body needs procedures and contracts for manufacturers' change notifications and assessing change significance. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.10 Surveillance activities and post-certification monitoringNotified body needs documented surveillance and post-certification monitoring procedures, including vigilance handling and surveillance audits. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.11 Re-certificationRe-certification at least every five years, using documented procedures and same methods as initial certification.
Annex VII 4.11(a) Renewal summary must cover all changes to the approved device. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.11(b) Renewal summary must include post-market surveillance experience. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.11(c) Renewal summary must include risk management experience. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.11(d) Renewal summary must include experience updating proof of Annex I compliance. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.11(e) Renewal summary must include clinical evaluation review experience, investigations and PMCF. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.11(f) Renewal summary must cover changes to requirements, components or scientific or regulatory environment. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.11(g) Renewal summary must cover changes to applied or new standards and specifications. Coming soon
Annex VII 4.11(h) Renewal summary must cover advances in medical, scientific and technical knowledge. Coming soon
Annex VIII CLASSIFICATION RULES
Annex VIII Chapter I DEFINITIONS SPECIFIC TO CLASSIFICATION RULES
Annex VIII 1 DURATION OF USEHeading for duration-of-use definitions.
Annex VIII 1.1 Defines transient use as continuous use under sixty minutes. Coming soon
Annex VIII 1.2 Defines short-term use as continuous use from sixty minutes to thirty days. Coming soon
Annex VIII 1.3 Defines long-term use as continuous use beyond thirty days. Coming soon
Annex VIII 2 INVASIVE AND ACTIVE DEVICESHeading for definitions of invasive and active devices.
Annex VIII 2.1 Defines body orifice as natural opening, eyeball surface or permanent artificial opening. Coming soon
Annex VIII 2.2 Defines surgically invasive device.
Annex VIII 2.2(a) Surgically invasive includes invasive devices penetrating the body surface during or through surgery. Coming soon
Annex VIII 2.2(b) Surgically invasive includes devices producing penetration other than through a body orifice. Coming soon
Annex VIII 2.3 Defines reusable surgical instrument as non-active cutting or similar tool intended for reuse after reprocessing. Coming soon
Annex VIII 2.4 Defines active therapeutic device as one supporting, modifying, replacing or restoring biological functions for treatment. Coming soon
Annex VIII 2.5 Defines active diagnostic or monitoring device as one supplying information on physiological conditions or illnesses. Coming soon
Annex VIII 2.6 Defines central circulatory system by listing specific major blood vessels. Coming soon
Annex VIII 2.7 Defines central nervous system as brain, meninges and spinal cord. Coming soon
Annex VIII 2.8 Defines injured skin or mucous membrane as areas with pathological change or wounds. Coming soon
Annex VIII Chapter II IMPLEMENTING RULES
Annex VIII 3.1 Device classification depends on the manufacturer's intended purpose. Coming soon
Annex VIII 3.2 Combined devices are classified separately, and accessories are classified in their own right. Coming soon
Annex VIII 3.3 Software driving or influencing a device takes that device's class; standalone software is classified separately. Coming soon
Annex VIII 3.4 Devices without a specific body-part use are classified by their most critical specified use. Coming soon
Annex VIII 3.5 When several rules apply, the strictest one giving the higher class prevails. Coming soon
Annex VIII 3.6 Introduces the meaning of continuous use when calculating duration of use.
Annex VIII 3.6(a) Continuous use covers whole use of one device, ignoring temporary interruptions or removal for cleaning. Coming soon
Annex VIII 3.6(b) Continuous use includes accumulated use of devices meant to be immediately replaced by the same type. Coming soon
Annex VIII 3.7 A device allows direct diagnosis if it diagnoses alone or gives decisive diagnostic information. Coming soon
Annex VIII Chapter III
Annex VIII 4 NON-INVASIVE DEVICESSection heading for classification rules on non-invasive devices.
Annex VIII 4.1 Rule 1Non-invasive devices default to class I unless a later rule applies. Coming soon
Annex VIII 4.2 Rule 2Non-invasive devices channelling or storing fluids for later introduction into the body are generally class IIa. Coming soon
Annex VIII 4.3 Rule 3Non-invasive devices altering composition of body fluids or tissues are class IIb or higher, with exceptions. Coming soon
Annex VIII 4.4 Rule 4Non-invasive devices touching injured skin or mucous membrane are classified by this rule's tiers. Coming soon
Annex VIII 5 INVASIVE DEVICESSection heading for classification rules on invasive devices.
Annex VIII 5.1 Rule 5Body-orifice invasive devices are classified by whether and to what class of active device they connect. Coming soon
Annex VIII 5.2 Rule 6Transient-use surgically invasive devices are class IIa unless listed exceptions apply. Coming soon
Annex VIII 5.3 Rule 7Short-term surgically invasive devices are class IIa unless listed exceptions apply. Coming soon
Annex VIII 5.4 Rule 8Implantable and long-term surgically invasive devices are class IIb unless exceptions apply. Coming soon
Annex VIII 6 ACTIVE DEVICESSection heading for classification rules on active devices.
Annex VIII 6.1 Rule 9Active therapeutic energy devices are class IIa, rising to IIb or III for hazardous or implant-related cases. Coming soon
Annex VIII 6.2 Rule 10Active diagnostic and monitoring devices are class IIa; ionizing radiation imaging devices are IIb. Coming soon
Annex VIII 6.3 Rule 11Software classification: decision-informing software is IIa or higher by impact, monitoring software IIa or IIb, else class I. Coming soon
Annex VIII 6.4 Rule 12Active devices administering or removing substances are IIa, IIb if potentially hazardous. Coming soon
Annex VIII 6.5 Rule 13All other active devices fall into class I. Coming soon
Annex VIII 7 SPECIAL RULESSection heading for special classification rules.
Annex VIII 7.1 Rule 14Devices with an integral ancillary medicinal substance are class III. Coming soon
Annex VIII 7.2 Rule 15Contraception and STD-prevention devices are class IIb, or III if implantable or long-term invasive. Coming soon
Annex VIII 7.3 Rule 16Contact lens care and device disinfection products are classed IIa or IIb by use. Coming soon
Annex VIII 7.4 Rule 17Devices recording X-ray diagnostic images are class IIa. Coming soon
Annex VIII 7.5 Rule 18Devices made from non-viable human or animal tissues are class III, with an intact-skin animal exception. Coming soon
Annex VIII 7.6 Rule 19Devices containing nanomaterial are classified according to its potential for internal exposure. Coming soon
Annex VIII 7.7 Rule 20Orifice devices administering inhaled medicines are IIa, or IIb when critical to efficacy or life-threatening conditions. Coming soon
Annex VIII 7.8 Rule 21Devices of absorbed or dispersed substances introduced via orifice or skin are classified by this rule. Coming soon
Annex VIII 7.9 Rule 22Therapeutic devices with integrated diagnostics driving patient management, like closed loops, are class III. Coming soon

Annex IX 5.1(b) Notified body may be asked to present its conclusions to the expert panel. Coming soon
